items.title: Traders attack Edo Consumer Protection Committee members over fake products
items.description: By Ozioruva Aliu – BENIN CITY Member of the Edo State Consumer Protection Committee led by its chairman, Osaro Culture Iyamu were, on Thursday, attacked by some beverage sellers while trying to enforce ban on sales of fake, adulterated and unauthorised drinks along Mission Road in Benin City, the state capital. The committee members were on a routine mission to the area when they noticed that some sellers were removing cartons, bottles and cans of drinks from their shelves on seeing the committee members. The infuriated sellers then prevented the committee members from accessing their shops to ensure that what they had were genuine products. Consequently, security agencies have invited beverage sellers, including Beverages and Alcohol Dealers Association, for a meeting over the incident. Iyamu alleged that his committee had been under pressure to compromise. But he vowed to ensure that the essence of the committee, which is to rid Edo markets of fake and adulterated products, was fulfilled. “We will continue to safeguard the health and protect the rights of consumers in line with the SHINE Agenda of Governor Monday Okpebholo.” Vanguard News The post Traders attack Edo Consumer Protection Committee members over fake products appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Samia and Sekou Nkrumah reveal how the 1966 Coup affected their late brother
items.description: Samia and Sekou Nkrumah have recounted how the 1966 coup that toppled their father, Ghana’s first President, Dr Kwame Nkrumah, deeply affected their late brother, Gamel Nkrumah. The two siblings shared aspects of Gamel’s life and the difficulties he experienced following the overthrow of the Nkrumah government, including the family’s years in exile and his struggles after returning to Ghana. Gamel, who spent much of his life in Egypt, was among the children of Dr Kwame Nkrumah who returned to Ghana with the family in 1975 after the government of the then Head of State, General Ignatius Kutu Acheampong, facilitated their return from exile. According to Sekou, Gamel struggled to settle into life in Ghana and encountered health challenges that disrupted his education. He said Gamel enrolled in a boarding school after the family returned but became seriously ill after about two months. The family subsequently adjusted his education plans, moving him and his brother Samuel from Form Five to Form Four. Gamel later attended A-Grid, where he was expected to pursue what Sekou described as “6-4”, but experienced further health difficulties. Sekou said the 1966 coup had particularly affected Gamel, whose experiences after the overthrow of their father’s government shaped much of his life. He also recounted that Gamel later studied and worked at the Institute of Development Studies in Harare, Zimbabwe, after securing an opportunity through the intervention of Sally Mugabe. The siblings shared these accounts when members of the Convention People’s Party (CPP), led by Comrade Chris Ziga, visited the Nkrumah family to express condolences following Gamel’s death. The delegation, comprising members of the party’s Council of Elders and National Working Committee, was received by Samia and Sekou Nkrumah. The family expressed appreciation to the governments of Ghana and Egypt for their support during Gamel’s hospitalisation and burial. The CPP delegation also pledged the party’s support for the family as it prepares for Gamel’s final funeral rites in Ghana.

items.title: Nigeria must deploy tollgates, technology to improve highway security – Musa
items.description: By Johnbosco Agbakwuru The Minister of Defence, General Christopher Musa (retd), has advocated restoring tollgates on major highways and deploying modern technology to enhance highway security and help identify and track criminals. Musa noted that tollgates could play a valuable security role, especially with modern technology that can identify and track vehicles without requiring drivers to stop for manual payments. The minister made the remarks at the Abuja roundtable, “Promise to Proof: The Renewed Hope Conversation,” organised by the APC Progressive Strategy Roundtable. It was convened by the Executive Chairman/CEO of PICNG and EVs, Ismaeel Ahmed. Responding to concerns about highway security and a suggestion that motorists could contribute through security levies at tollgates, Musa described the reintroduction of tollgates as a good idea, noting that Nigeria might have made a mistake by dismantling them. He explained that modern tolling systems in other countries use technology to identify vehicles through their registration numbers, with payments processed electronically, adding that such systems could also assist security agencies in identifying and tracking vehicles. The minister also called for the strengthening of Nigeria’s identification system through the use of personal identification numbers, facial recognition and fingerprints to improve security monitoring. He said technology would make it easier for security agencies to establish people’s identities and track criminal activities. On the broader security situation, Musa said the Federal Government was recording progress in tackling terrorism, banditry and kidnapping through increased defence investment, improved intelligence gathering, joint military operations and stronger cooperation among security agencies. He disclosed that the Federal Government allocated ₦5.4 trillion to defence in the 2026 budget and was recruiting an additional 12,000 military personnel to strengthen manpower and security coverage. According to him, the government was also investing in modern weapons, surveillance systems and operational platforms to improve intelligence gathering, mobility, firepower and rapid response capabilities. He further disclosed that Nigerian security forces killed more than 300 terrorists and bandits, including over 10 commanders, in operations conducted in the week preceding his presentation. The minister identified porous borders as a major challenge, noting that Nigeria shares extensive borders with neighbouring countries, particularly Niger Republic, through which criminal groups and illicit arms can move. He said the government was strengthening border security and expanding bilateral, regional and international defence cooperation through intelligence sharing, specialised training and technological support. Musa added that Nigeria continued to maintain security relationships with Niger, Burkina Faso and Mali despite their withdrawal from ECOWAS, including military training and cooperation around border areas. He warned that instability in the Sahel posed a serious threat to West Africa and urged regional countries to work together to prevent the collapse of neighbouring states. The minister also highlighted the importance of local defence manufacturing, disclosing that the government had strengthened the country’s defence industry through legislative reforms and partnerships with equipment manufacturers. He said Nigeria recently hosted the first African International Military Defence Exhibition, which attracted 63 countries and provided opportunities for local manufacturers to meet international partners and sign investment agreements. According to him, domestic production of military equipment would reduce dependence on foreign suppliers, create employment and generate foreign exchange. He called on Nigerians with expertise in cybersecurity, drone manufacturing and other defence technologies to bring forward their ideas for possible collaboration with the Defence Industry Corporation of Nigeria. Addressing concerns about the increasing involvement of the military in internal security operations, Musa acknowledged that soldiers had become overstretched by prolonged deployments across the country. He said the military’s involvement was necessary in situations where security challenges exceeded the capacity of the police but stressed that the armed forces were working to strengthen police capacity to enable soldiers to gradually return to their primary responsibilities. According to him, the military was already assisting the police while the government pursued additional recruitment, equipment procurement and institutional reforms. He disclosed that security agencies were enjoying unprecedented cooperation, describing the current level of interagency coordination as a significant improvement. Musa also highlighted the role of communities in combating insecurity, urging Nigerians to report suspicious activities rather than remain indifferent. He said criminals often operated within communities and depended on local support, adding that security agencies could not succeed without the cooperation of citizens. The minister cited community-based intelligence and the use of civilian joint task forces as important components of the security strategy, noting that local residents could provide timely information to security operatives. He also disclosed that the military was working with forest rangers and other community-based security structures to protect farmers and enable agricultural activities to continue in vulnerable areas. On the welfare of military personnel, the minister said the government had increased soldiers’ salaries and was improving their living conditions, healthcare and operational support. He recalled that a private soldier previously earned about ₦49,000 monthly before the amount was increased to approximately ₦100,000 and subsequently to nearly ₦200,000. He said military personnel and their families were entitled to free medical treatment, adding that soldiers requiring specialised treatment could be flown abroad. Musa also explained that military personnel underwent psychological preparation before deployment and assessment after operations to address the effects of traumatic experiences. He said returning soldiers were monitored for psychological challenges, including post-traumatic stress disorder, anger and other behavioural changes. According to him, military personnel could undergo two to three weeks of post-deployment assessment and support before returning to their families and units. He added that the military provided support systems for soldiers’ spouses and families, including access to loans, medical care and educational assistance for their children. On fallen military personnel, Musa said their families were entitled to salaries, allowances and other benefits, while their children were supported through university education. He stressed that caring for injured soldiers and families of fallen heroes was essential to maintaining the morale and commitment of troops serving in dangerous conditions. Also speaking at the roundtable, the Executive Secretary of the Nigerian Police Trust Fund, Alhaji Mohamed Shaidou, said the Federal Government was addressing longstanding challenges in police funding, training, equipment and welfare. Shaidou said the police had suffered years of underfunding and neglect, making it difficult for the force to effectively discharge its responsibility of maintaining internal security and enforcing the law. He explained that the Nigerian Police Trust Fund was established as an intervention agency to support police training, equipment procurement and officers’ welfare. He said the current administration had placed greater emphasis on strengthening policing, adding that the government had also begun considering ways to improve funding through the proposed establishment of state police. According to him, the government approved about ₦100 billion for the rehabilitation of police training institutions following an assessment of training facilities across the country. He said the Trust Fund was also investing in continuous training, police stations, operational vehicles, bulletproof vests and other equipment required by officers. Shaidou argued that improving police training institutions was particularly important because officers needed the right professional and mental preparation before being deployed to protect lives and maintain law and order. He also disclosed that the Trust Fund had entered into partnerships with the Rural Electrification Agency (REA), the National Agricultural Land Development Authority (NALDA) and Family Homes Funds to improve the welfare of police officers and their dependants. Under the housing initiative, he said the Trust Fund was working towards providing 1,000 housing units per state for police officers to enable them to own their homes. He disclosed that a groundbreaking ceremony had already been conducted for about 250 housing units in Nasarawa State. Shaidou said the Trust Fund was also working with the REA to provide electricity for housing projects and police facilities. He revealed that some smart police stations had been equipped with off-grid solar power systems to ensure that their operations were not disrupted by electricity challenges. On transportation, he said the Trust Fund had introduced welfare buses to convey police officers in Abuja from locations including Mararaba, Zuba and other communities to their duty posts. He said the initiative was designed to reduce the financial burden on officers who previously spent their personal resources commuting to work. He acknowledged contributions towards the transportation initiative, including the donation of a 40-seater bus and a 50-seater bus to support police transportation. The Trust Fund, he added, was considering the use of compressed natural gas (CNG) buses to reduce fuel and maintenance costs and ensure the sustainability of the programme. Shaidou further disclosed that the Fund had partnered with NALDA to provide agricultural opportunities for dependants of police officers. He said the initiative would enable families of officers to access farmland and engage in farming as an additional source of income and food supply. He explained that discussions had already commenced with governors of Kano and Niger states on the programme. On the proposed establishment of state police, Shaidou said the Trust Fund supported the initiative but stressed the need to strengthen the existing federal police structure. He argued that countries operating state police systems also maintained federal police institutions, adding that Nigeria must ensure its federal police force was adequately strengthened as the country considers the proposed reform. Earlier, participants at the roundtable raised concerns about the protection of citizens who provide security intelligence, particularly whistleblowers who fear possible exposure or retaliation. Responding, Musa said the protection of informants was important and encouraged Nigerians to continue providing credible intelligence to security agencies. He also said the Defence Ministry and military service headquarters received correspondence from citizens and were working towards establishing an emergency reporting line to facilitate the transmission of security information. Participants equally called for stronger collaboration between security agencies and private-sector organisations, particularly in the power sector, to provide reliable electricity for local defence manufacturing. Musa welcomed the proposal, describing energy supply as a major challenge facing defence manufacturers, and pledged to connect the relevant parties for further engagement. The minister also urged Nigerians to promote national unity, saying the country’s security challenges required collective responsibility beyond religious, ethnic and regional differences. He maintained that the ultimate measure of security success should be farmers returning to their farms, travellers moving safely on highways, markets reopening and businesses operating without fear. The post Nigeria must deploy tollgates, technology to improve highway security – Musa appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Tesla y SpaceX pierden 417.000 millones de valor en dos días tras el triunfo demócrata
items.description: Las elecciones de mitad de mandato han supuesto un fuerte revolcón para Donald Trump y su Partido Republicano. También para uno de sus grandes valedores, el empresario Elon Musk. Las dos grandes compañías controladas por Musk —Tesla y SpaceX— han sufrido una fuerte corrección bursátil tras la victoria inesperada de los demócratas en el estado de Texas y su mayoría en el Congreso de Estados Unidos. Las acciones de Tesla cayeron el miércoles un 3,3%, y este jueves han acelerado el desplome, con otro 10,77%. Las de SpaceX recortaron el primer día un 3,8% y este jueves otro 9%. En total, la pérdida de valor de mercado roza los 469.000 millones de dólares entre las dos compañías. Unos 417.000 millones de euros al tipo de cambio actual. CPP Elders visit Nkrumah family to console them over death of Gamel Nkrumah
items.description: A delegation from the Convention People’s Party (CPP), led by Comrade Chris Ziga, has visited the family of Ghana’s first President, Dr Kwame Nkrumah, to express condolences following the death of his second son, Gamel Nkrumah. The delegation comprised members of the party’s Council of Elders and National Working Committee. Receiving the delegation, Madam Samia Nkrumah and Sekou Nkrumah expressed sadness over the loss of their brother, who spent much of his life in Egypt. The family recounted how Gamel’s life was shaped by the 1966 coup that toppled their father’s government and forced them into exile. They said that although the family was formally invited back to Ghana by the Acheampong government in 1975, Gamel’s return was short-lived. Sekou Nkrumah explained that the experience of exile and the circumstances surrounding the family’s return affected Gamel deeply. Sekou said the 1966 coup had affected all the Nkrumah children but had a particularly profound impact on Gamel. “To understand Gamel very well, I think Samuel was right that the coup affected him. It affected all of us, but I think him in more ways,” he said. He recalled that after the family returned to Ghana in 1975, they settled in a house built in 1976. Gamel was enrolled in boarding school but reportedly became seriously ill after two months, prompting the family to reconsider his education. “After two months, Gamel got very sick. He had a nervous breakdown,” Sekou recounted. He said the illness affected the brothers’ academic progression, with Gamel and Samuel moving to Form Four rather than proceeding to Form Five. Sekou added that Gamel later continued his education at A-Grid, although he subsequently became ill again. According to Sekou, Gamel eventually moved abroad and spent several years in Zimbabwe, where he secured employment at the Institute of Development Studies through the assistance of Sally Mugabe. “He was offered a job through Sally Mugabe. He was offered a job in the Institute of Development Studies in Harare. So he went to live there for a few years,” he said. Gamel later spent much of his life in Egypt, where the Nkrumah family had found refuge following the 1966 coup. The family disclosed that Gamel had been unwell for some time and expressed appreciation to the governments of Ghana and Egypt for their support during his hospitalisation and burial. The CPP delegation assured the family of the party’s continued support, particularly when arrangements are made for Gamel’s final funeral rites in Ghana. Gamel Nkrumah was the second son of Ghana’s first President, Dr Kwame Nkrumah. He died recently after a period of illness. The family is expected to announce arrangements for his final funeral rites in Ghana in due course.

items.title: The Ballad of Bob Dylan and the Pope
items.description: At first, the image appears to be some kind of intergalactic photo op, something out of Star Wars . A figure hooded in black, his craggy face partly in shadow, greets a serene-looking man in a white robe. Think Emperor Palpatine shaking hands with Obi-Wan Kenobi, perhaps brokering a cease-fire in the Clone Wars. Closer inspection yields a picture that is no less weird: Bob Dylan is hanging with the pope. What they actually spoke about during their meeting yesterday at the Vatican’s Apostolic Palace, we may never know. But the questions only begin there! Why is Dylan’s head covered by a hood? Why, in some photos, does he have gloves and an umbrella? Why does he seem to have abandoned tying his polka-dotted tie mid-flip? And: Is the pope a fan? (Actually, that last one might have an answer—in a recent book about disarmament, the pope quoted Dylan’s 1963 deep cut “Go Away You Bomb”; “I want that Bomb—I want it settin in my mouth like a cigar,” goes one line. This is unfiltered Dylan that only a true fan could love.) The most famous American musician of the past half century visits the leader of the Catholic Church. The strangeness, if not the Sith hood, makes you laugh. But these two make some sense together, if not as obvious friends then at least, each in their own way, as spiritually ambitious people. Also, they are both midwestern Bobs. Robert Zimmerman, born in Duluth, Minnesota, in 1941, meet Robert Francis Prevost, born in Chicago in 1955. They share the common matter-of-factness of people who grew up on the flat plains, who were born in the middle. There is no frenetic city energy to them. They even have similarly enigmatic smiles—lips tight in a straight line, not giving away too much. Their gifts to each other were pretty unfussy, too. Dylan handed the pope a copy of his memoir, Chronicles: Volume One , and the pope gave Dylan—of course—a rosary. [ Read: The pope doubles down on the beautiful struggle ] From their middle-class, conventional Middle American upbringings, they both embarked on wild transformations. Dylan used traditional American music to mold himself into a troubadour from nowhere. He abandoned his given name, invented a mythology around his origins, and still resists definition. Prevost had a different kind of reinvention. He joined an ancient religious order, submitted himself to its disciplines, and ultimately assumed an identity set by its history, losing his name to become the pope. Two midwestern-American boys, avatars of self-transformation, now aged but still happily wearing costumes. But there’s more: In a moment when so many people are worried about how artificial intelligence is flattening human expression, could there be anything more affirming of human uniqueness than the life and work of Dylan and the pope? Even Dylan’s idiosyncratic outfit was the product of ingenuity that a computer couldn’t dream of matching, if computers could dream. The workwear designer Gauthier Borsarello instantly spotted that the jacket was his own creation. “The good thing about designing everything (even the puller of your zipper) from scratch is recognizing your own design without a doubt,” Borsarello wrote on Instagram. The pope, meanwhile, has become one of the most eloquent defenders of human creativity in the face of technological advance. His encyclical, Magnifica Humanitas , published this year, articulated beautifully why human limitations and our efforts to overcome them make us special and give our lives meaning. “Authentic culture and art” preserve a “spark,” he wrote; they allow people to take in the experiences of others, all the vulnerability and pain, and reflect them back in ways that elevate, resulting in Beethoven’s Ninth Symphony and Picasso’s Guernica . (And why not “Subterranean Homesick Blues”?—though the pope sadly didn’t put this on his list of faves.) And then there’s Dylan. Perhaps no other artist has reveled for so long in mixing and matching as much as he does, ingesting enormous quantities of cultural material, breaking them into pieces, and recombining them into something new. That’s been his whole schtick, from the beginning. In a way it anticipates what AI has supercharged, but he does it as only a human can, informed by a lifetime of listening, reading, performing, and inhabiting the American cultural imagination. [ Read: Rock and roll faces the inevitable ] Take “A Hard Rain’s a-Gonna Fall,” from 1962. In it, he riffs on the question-and-answer structure from a traditional English-Scottish border ballad called “Lord Randall” (“Oh where ha’e ye been, Lord Randall, my son? O where ha’e ye been, my handsome young man?”). But Dylan infuses the form with surreal, apocalyptic imagery related to the Cold War and the anxiety of annihilation: “And what did you hear, my blue-eyed son? And what did you hear, my darling young one? I heard the sound of a thunder, it roared out a warnin’. Heard the roar of a wave that could drown the whole world.” Only the synapses of his weird brain could produce this. In his 2001 album, Love and Theft (an aptly titled middle finger to anyone who has a problem with this method), he lifts whole sentences from Confessions of a Yakuza , the memoir of a Japanese gangster. I’d like to think this is the question Dylan and the pope, sitting next to bookcases full of Catholic exegesis, discussed: What makes humans worth preserving? The photo of them is indelible because it’s sort of the answer. They’re dressed in black and in white, the whole spectrum of good to evil. One’s an artist and the other’s a priest, each aspiring to prophecy. They’re both accessing something larger than themselves, even though when you look at them, they’re small, old men, nearer to the end of their existences than to the beginning—the pope battling cancer, and Dylan in his mid-80s. The spark, however, persists.

IPT | Dr Emna Harigua remporte le Pasteur network talent award 2026
items.description: Dr Emna Harigua a reçu le Pasteur Network Talent Award 2026 – AI Edition, le mercredi 4 novembre, à l’occasion de la réunion annuelle du Pasteur Network (PNAM), organisée à Laval, au Canada. Cette distinction revêt une importance particulière puisque l'édition 2026 est la première à être spécifiquement consacrée à l'intelligence artificielle (IA), soulignant le rôle croissant de cette technologie dans la transformation de la recherche biomédicale et la réponse aux grands défis mondiaux de santé. Les Pasteur Network Talent Awards visent à reconnaître et à soutenir les talents scientifiques du réseau, tout en encourageant la recherche innovante, l'excellence scientifique et le leadership. La sélection est particulièrement compétitive. Les candidatures sont évaluées selon la qualité des travaux de recherche, l'originalité et le potentiel d'impact du projet proposé, ainsi que la capacité des candidats à présenter et à communiquer leur vision scientifique. Dr Emna Harigua a été sélectionnée comme lauréate de l'édition 2026 dédiée à l'IA, en reconnaissance de ses travaux à l'interface de l'intelligence artificielle, de la bioinformatique structurale et de la modélisation moléculaire appliquées à la découverte de médicaments. Ce prix vient soutenir son projet « AI-Driven Medicinal Chemistry for Next-Generation Anti-Leishmania Drug Design ». À la tête d'une équipe de recherche à l'Institut Pasteur de Tunis, Dr Harigua développe des approches computationnelles innovantes intégrant l'intelligence artificielle pour accélérer l'identification de nouveaux candidats thérapeutiques, avec un intérêt particulier pour les maladies infectieuses. IPT L’article IPT | Dr Emna Harigua remporte le Pasteur network talent award 2026 est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: Kwadaso Agric College students turn ideas into market-ready agribusiness under CB-VET Ghana project
items.description: Innovation, entrepreneurship and practical skills are increasingly becoming the foundation of modern Agricultural Technical and Vocational Education and Training (ATVET) in Ghana, a shift clearly demonstrated by the CB-VET Ghana Project. For the past three years, over 500 students of Kwadaso Agricultural College, under the VET Ecosystems for Employability in Ghana (CB-VET) initiative, have embarked on an intensive entrepreneurship and business incubation journey. This has culminated in the successful development, implementation and exhibition of market-ready and eco-friendly agribusiness products. Through the project, lecturers were trained in modern teaching methods, business incubation and industry engagement, while students were exposed to hands-on product development, costing, branding, packaging and pitching of business ideas to potential investors and partners. From processed foods and packaged farm produce to digital farming solutions and climate-smart innovations, the exhibition showcased what students can achieve when classroom learning is deliberately linked to business development, mentorship and real market demands. The VET Ecosystems for Employability in Ghana (CB-VET) project is a major milestone of the European Union-funded Erasmus+ initiative, which spanned from December 2023 to November 2026, and now modernised to ATVET. The project utilizes frameworks like the Business Model Canvas (BMC) to help training centres build income-generating services. In his address as the project ends, Principal of Kwadaso Agric College, Albert Appiah Amoako, revealed that the entrepreneurship programme was deliberately designed as a joint intervention to strengthen ATVET by making agriculture education more practical, entrepreneurial, digitally responsive and aligned with industry and labour-market needs. He said the project addresses the need for skilled agricultural graduates who can respond to climate change, modern agricultural technologies, food processing and the growing demand for sustainable agribusinesses. According to Mr. Appiah Amoako, the program promoted stronger collaboration among vocational training institutions, industry, government agencies and other stakeholders to improve graduate employability and entrepreneurship. “The traditional model of agricultural education, which focused heavily on theory and production alone, no longer meets the needs of today’s agricultural economy,” Mr. Amoako noted. “Employers now require graduates who can process, package, market, manage businesses and apply digital tools to solve farm and agribusiness problems.” He added that the project has helped reposition the school not only as a training school, but as a hub for innovation, incubation and enterprise development for young people interested in agriculture. Highlighting the key achievements and outputs, the Vice Principal of the college, Dr. Ishak Shaibu, said the project fostered industry-education collaboration between training institutions, private enterprises, public institutions and other agricultural stakeholders to ensure that training responds to real industry needs. He further noted that the CB-VET Ghana promoted entrepreneurial learning, practical business development and a stronger link between agricultural education and employment opportunities. Senior Project Consultant at Maastricht School of Management (MSM), Hans Nijhoff, highlighted that the program equipped students and trainers with skills in Climate-Smart Agriculture (CSA) production, agro-food processing and digital farming technologies. Mr. Nijhoff said the emphasis on climate-smart production is particularly important, as farmers and agribusinesses must adapt to changing weather patterns, soil degradation and rising production costs, while still meeting growing demand for food. “By linking training directly to private-sector needs, the project has helped reduce the mismatch between what graduates learn in school and what employers and the market actually require,” he said. Ashanti Regional Director of Agriculture, Dr. David Anambam, emphasized on the essence of agriculture to Ghana’s economy, its contribution to food and nutrition security, employment, income generation and rural development. However, he said the sector is evolving rapidly due to climate change, technological advancement, changing market demands and the need for sustainable production systems. He described the initiative as timely, saying it had strengthened ATVET and made agricultural education more responsive to the changing needs of the sector. “Training institutions must therefore produce graduates who are not only knowledgeable but also technically competent, innovative, entrepreneurial and capable of addressing real-world challenges,” he urged. He commended the European Union for its support through the Erasmus+ Capacity Building in Vocational Education and Training programme, as well as Ghanaian and European partners for their collaboration. The Product Exhibition and Business Pitch Competition wrapped up three years of intense learning, but also kicked off many entrepreneurial ventures. Several showcased business concepts have major commercial potential and will keep getting mentorship, networking and incubation support through the CB-VET Ghana project.

items.title: Protection des travailleurs en Guinée : voici la liste des 92 maladies professionnelles indemnisables
items.description: Le président de la République, Mamadi Doumbouya, a signé, ce jeudi 5 novembre 2026, un décret fixant la liste officielle des maladies professionnelles indemnisables en République de Guinée. Cette mesure vise à renforcer la protection sociale des travailleurs, en encadrant davantage la reconnaissance et l’indemnisation des pathologies liées à l’exercice d’une activité professionnelle. Diffusé à la télévision nationale, le décret recense 92 infections ou groupes d’infections, répartis en quatre grandes catégories. Il s’agit notamment des maladies provoquées par des agents chimiques, physiques ou biologiques, ainsi que des affections touchant certains organes et fonctions de l’organisme. Désormais, les maladies reconnues comme étant directement liées à l’exercice d’une activité professionnelle et figurant dans les tableaux officiels pourront donner droit à une prise en charge et à une indemnisation, sous réserve du respect des conditions prévues par la réglementation. Chaque tableau précise notamment les manifestations cliniques exigées, les délais de prise en charge ainsi que les types de travaux susceptibles d’exposer les travailleurs aux risques concernés. Le texte prévoit également la mise en place d’une Commission nationale permanente de révision, placée sous la tutelle des ministères en charge du Travail et de la Santé. Cette instance aura pour mission de suivre l’évolution des risques professionnels, de recenser les nouvelles pathologies liées au travail et de proposer, si nécessaire, une actualisation de la réglementation à la lumière des avancées scientifiques, sanitaires et technologiques. En abrogeant toutes les dispositions antérieures contraires, le décret entre en vigueur dès sa date de signature. Il établit ainsi un nouveau cadre réglementaire pour la reconnaissance et l’indemnisation des maladies professionnelles en Guinée, avec pour objectif de mieux protéger la santé et les droits des travailleurs.

items.title: Alerte météo – Guinée : Une vague de chaleur annoncée jusqu’au 18 novembre
items.description: L’Agence nationale de la météorologie (ANM) a lancé une alerte à la vague de chaleur sur l’ensemble du territoire guinéen, pour la période du 4 au 18 novembre 2026 . Dans son bulletin publié ce jeudi 5 novembre, l’institution évoque une situation de gravité élevée, avec des températures diurnes et nocturnes anormalement élevées. Selon l’ANM, cette vague de chaleur est observée depuis le début du mois d’octobre en Basse-Guinée, en Haute-Guinée ainsi que dans plusieurs localités de la Moyenne-Guinée. Au cours des quinze prochains jours, le phénomène devrait se maintenir, s’étendre aux autres régions du pays et s’intensifier par endroits. L’agence prévient que cette situation pourrait entraîner des risques sanitaires importants, notamment le stress thermique et la déshydratation. Elle souligne également que la demande en énergie devrait rester particulièrement élevée durant cette période.

items.title: Maladies professionnelles : le président Mamadi Doumbouya instaure un nouveau cadre d’indemnisation en Guinée
items.description: Le président de la République, Mamadi Doumbouya, a signé ce jeudi 5 novembre 2026 un décret fixant la liste officielle des maladies professionnelles indemnisables en République de Guinée. Cette décision vise à renforcer la protection sociale des travailleurs et à mieux encadrer la reconnaissance et l’indemnisation des pathologies liées à l’exercice d’une activité professionnelle. Diffusé à la télévision nationale, le décret répertorie 92 infections ou groupes d’infections répartis en quatre grandes catégories, notamment celles provoquées par des agents chimiques, physiques et biologiques, ainsi que les maladies affectant certains organes et fonctions de l’organisme. Désormais, les affections reconnues comme étant directement liées à l’activité professionnelle et inscrites dans les tableaux officiels pourront ouvrir droit à une prise en charge et à une indemnisation, conformément aux conditions prévues. Chaque tableau précise notamment les symptômes requis, les délais de prise en charge ainsi que les travaux susceptibles d’entraîner l’exposition aux risques concernés. Le décret prévoit également la création d’une Commission nationale permanente de révision, placée sous la tutelle des ministères chargés du Travail et de la Santé. Cette structure aura pour mission de suivre l’évolution des risques professionnels, d’identifier les nouvelles pathologies liées au travail et de proposer des actualisations de la réglementation en fonction des évolutions scientifiques, sanitaires et technologiques. En abrogeant toutes les dispositions antérieures contraires, ce nouveau texte entre en vigueur dès sa date de signature. Il constitue une nouvelle étape dans le renforcement du dispositif de protection sociale et sanitaire des travailleurs guinéens.

items.title: Ghana, Trinidad and Tobago explore new investments, expanded oil and gas partnerships
items.description: Ghana and Trinidad and Tobago are seeking to deepen their economic relations, with fresh discussions focusing on attracting new investments and expanding cooperation in the oil and gas sector. The Minister for Foreign Affairs, Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa, held discussions with his Trinidad and Tobago counterpart, Sean S.M. Sobers, on the sidelines of the just-ended Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM) in Antigua and Barbuda. The meeting provided an opportunity for both countries to assess progress in their bilateral relations and explore new areas of economic cooperation. Mr Ablakwa said the discussions centred on strengthening investment ties and expanding existing partnerships in the oil and gas industry. As part of efforts to deepen diplomatic relations, Ghana is expected to commission its new High Commission in Trinidad and Tobago next year. The mission will be headed by William Anani Abotsi, who is expected to become Ghana’s first High Commissioner to the Caribbean nation. Beyond its bilateral engagements, Ghana also used its participation at the Commonwealth meeting to advance discussions on issues affecting Africa and the wider international community. These included reforms to the United Nations, the reconfiguration of the international financial architecture, artificial intelligence regulation, climate justice, resource sovereignty, reparatory justice and conflict resolution. The engagements form part of Ghana’s broader diplomatic efforts to strengthen relations with international partners while advancing Africa’s interests in global governance.

items.title: I’m surprised I haven’t won TGMA Rapper of the Year – Teephlow
items.description: For a rapper who has earned multiple nominations at Ghana’s biggest music awards, never taking home the Rapper of the Year trophy is a record Teephlow finds difficult to understand. He has admitted that he is surprised he is yet to win the Telecel Ghana Music Awards (TGMA) Rapper of the Year title, despite his unbeatable records. Speaking in an interview with Kwame Dadzie on Hitz FM , Teephlow said he does not usually keep track of past nominations or make music with awards in mind. However, he said one thing that has stayed with him is the fact that he remains the only rapper among those nominated alongside him who has never won the category. “I can say one thing I’m surprised about is the fact that, of all the people who have been nominated, I’m the only one who hasn’t won Best Rapper before. And it’s almost shocking if you really think about it,” he said. He questioned whether his record meant he had somehow fallen short of the standard expected of a Best Rapper winner, although he added that he no longer allows the issue to weigh on him. Teephlow also used the interview to question how winners in the category are selected, arguing that streaming numbers should not be the measure of an artiste’s lyrical ability or impact. For him, the award should look beyond how many times a song is played and consider the quality of an artiste’s body of work, lyrical skill, the message in the music and the influence it has on listeners. He proposed that the awards scheme could consider having separate judging teams for technical categories such as Rapper of the Year and broader categories such as Artiste of the Year, arguing that the skills required to assess each are different. Teephlow said he would welcome the opportunity to contribute to such discussions if he were ever invited to be part of the teams responsible for shaping the process. While he insists awards are not what drive his music, his comments show that the absence of a TGMA Rapper of the Year trophy remains one career milestone he finds surprising. According to the Telecel Ghana Music Awards, the Best Rap Performance on a solo or collaborative song is adjudged by the Academy and the Board as the best word compositions or lyrical content, structure, rhymes, dexterity, and/or musical presentation reflecting the broad spectrum of rap music style and culture on a song, commercially released in the year under review. The song may not have enjoyed commercial success but must have good artistic value.

items.title: XPENG L03 : Smeia prépare l’arrivée de la technologie REEV au Maroc
items.description: Le Groupe Smeia prépare l’arrivée de la XPENG L03 sur le marché marocain. Ce nouveau modèle adopte la technologie REEV, qui associe propulsion électrique et prolongateur d’autonomie, avec jusqu’à 215 km d’autonomie électrique et 1 017 km d’autonomie combinée annoncée selon le cycle WLTP. Les premières livraisons sont prévues à partir de décembre 2026. Le Groupe Smeia, importateur et distributeur officiel de XPENG au Maroc, annonce l’arrivée prochaine de la XPENG L03, un modèle équipé de la technologie REEV ( Range-Extended Electric Vehicle ). Cette architecture de motorisation, déjà développée dans le secteur automobile, permet d’associer les avantages de la conduite électrique à une autonomie étendue, offrant ainsi une alternative aux automobilistes souhaitant bénéficier de la propulsion électrique sans dépendre exclusivement des infrastructures de recharge pour leurs longs trajets. Les précommandes ont été lancées en octobre 2026, tandis que les premières livraisons sont attendues à partir de décembre. La technologie REEV, entre conduite électrique et autonomie étendue Contrairement à un véhicule hybride classique, la technologie REEV repose sur une propulsion assurée par un moteur électrique. Le moteur thermique ne transmet pas directement sa puissance aux roues : il fonctionne comme un générateur pour produire de l’électricité lorsque la batterie doit être soutenue. Cette architecture permet de conserver les sensations de conduite propres à la motorisation électrique, notamment une accélération réactive et une conduite fluide, tout en limitant les contraintes liées à l’autonomie lors des déplacements de longue distance. Le dispositif vise également à préserver le confort acoustique et à limiter les vibrations associées au fonctionnement du prolongateur d’autonomie. L’objectif est de proposer une expérience de conduite électrique adaptée aussi bien aux trajets quotidiens qu’aux déplacements plus longs. Jusqu’à 1 017 km d’autonomie annoncée La XPENG L03 affiche une autonomie électrique de 215 km selon le cycle WLTP. Cette capacité permet d’envisager une utilisation électrique sur une part importante des déplacements quotidiens, selon les habitudes de conduite et les conditions réelles d’utilisation. Pour les trajets plus longs, l’autonomie combinée annoncée atteint 1 017 km selon le cycle WLTP, grâce à l’association de la batterie rechargeable et du prolongateur d’autonomie. Cette configuration vise à offrir davantage de flexibilité aux conducteurs qui souhaitent bénéficier de la propulsion électrique tout en conservant une plus grande liberté de déplacement. Sur le plan des performances, le modèle développe une puissance maximale annoncée de 240 chevaux. Il passe de 0 à 100 km/h en 6,8 secondes et affiche une vitesse maximale de 180 km/h. La recharge rapide en courant continu permet, selon les données communiquées, de passer de 30 % à 80 % de batterie en 16 minutes, sous réserve de la puissance disponible et des conditions de recharge. Connectivité, technologies embarquées et confort à bord Au-delà de sa motorisation, la XPENG L03 mise sur un équipement technologique destiné à améliorer l’expérience à bord et à faciliter les déplacements quotidiens. L’habitacle accueille notamment un écran tactile central de 15,6 pouces , qui donne accès aux principales fonctionnalités du véhicule et à son interface numérique. La connectivité embarquée constitue également un élément important de l’équipement, avec des fonctionnalités pensées pour faciliter l'interaction entre le conducteur, son véhicule et les services numériques. Le confort des occupants est également mis en avant grâce à des sièges chauffants et ventilés , permettant d’adapter les conditions d’assise aux différentes saisons. Un affichage tête haute complète l’environnement technologique du conducteur, tandis que l'éclairage d'ambiance contribue à l'atmosphère intérieure. Sur le volet de la sécurité, le modèle est annoncé avec sept airbags. L’assistance automatique au stationnement figure également parmi les équipements mentionnés. Avec un coffre de 539 litres , la XPENG L03 offre par ailleurs un volume de rangement adapté aux besoins du quotidien comme aux déplacements de longue distance. Le véhicule dispose également de points d’ancrage pour barres de toit , permettant l’installation de barres adaptées pour transporter des équipements et des bagages supplémentaires. Cette dotation entend ainsi combiner connectivité, confort, espace et praticité dans un véhicule qui cherche à répondre aux attentes d’une clientèle sensible aux nouvelles solutions de mobilité. Smeia renforce l’offre XPENG au Maroc L’arrivée de la XPENG L03 s’inscrit dans la stratégie de développement du Groupe Smeia, qui accompagne l’implantation de la marque chinoise sur le marché marocain. Avec la technologie REEV, le distributeur enrichit son offre d’une solution intermédiaire entre le véhicule électrique à batterie et les motorisations thermiques traditionnelles. L’enjeu est de répondre aux attentes des automobilistes en matière d’autonomie, de confort et de flexibilité, dans un contexte où les nouvelles technologies de propulsion prennent une place croissante dans le secteur automobile. Les premières livraisons de la XPENG L03 sont prévues à partir de décembre 2026. Les caractéristiques annoncées, notamment l’autonomie, les performances et les équipements, restent à considérer selon les spécifications définitives de la version commercialisée au Maroc. items.title: Italian chef sacked for refusing to put pineapple on pizza, says it insulted his culture
items.description: An Italian chef in Australia has lost an unfair dismissal claim after being sacked for, among other workplace issues, refusing to serve ham and pineapple pizza, describing the topping as an insult to his culture. Davide Tamburella was dismissed from the now-closed La Costa restaurant in Brisbane in May, following a meeting with management over several complaints about his conduct. One of the issues raised was his refusal to prepare ham and pineapple pizzas for guests attending an event at the restaurant. According to a ruling by Australia’s Fair Work Commission, Tamburella argued that instructions from management “need not be followed when it is offensive to his culture”. The commission noted that the chef’s objection to the fruit was because “he considers, as an Italian, that putting pineapple on a pizza is an insult to his culture”. It also found that this was not the first time he had refused to use pineapple on pizzas, recording three such instances over four years. On a previous occasion, Tamburella had asked his employer to “check how important it is for Italians not to put pineapple on a pizza”. Beyond the dispute over pizza toppings, management raised concerns about his use of foul language, communication style and what it described as an “escalation of frustration in the workplace”. The ruling also detailed an incident in April when Tamburella fractured bones in his right hand after striking a metal handrail at work. The chef had reportedly hoped to secure employer sponsorship for a visa that would allow him to remain in Australia as a permanent resident. However, following his dismissal, the restaurant discontinued the sponsorship process. Tamburella subsequently approached the Fair Work Commission, challenging his dismissal. However, the commission rejected his unfair dismissal claim because it was lodged outside the permitted timeframe. The restaurant’s managing director, Elliot Ingram, told the Daily Mail there was “more to this story than a pizza topping”. The BBC said it had contacted Tamburella for comment. On his LinkedIn profile, the chef describes himself as someone whose career has focused on “delivering exceptional food” and “improving business performance”. He also shared a post titled “letter for chefs” three months ago, centred on the theme of “respecting the ingredients”. His LinkedIn profile indicates that he now works at another restaurant in Brisbane. A BBC check found that pineapple is not included on its menu. Meanwhile, Queensland, where the restaurant was located, is regarded as Australia’s pineapple heartland and produces the country’s commercially grown pineapples. The state is also home to the Big Pineapple, a 16-metre fibreglass structure on the Sunshine Coast that has become a popular local landmark. items.title: This Won’t Be Easy for Democrats
items.description: James Talarico talked a lot during his campaign about the so-called wilderness—as in, the electoral wasteland and morale morass that Democrats had been languishing in since President Trump’s reelection, in 2024. In Texas, this felt like something of a permanent condition. Talarico preferred a more sanguine interpretation of wilderness, something I’ve thought about after he became the first Texas Democrat to win a Senate race since 1988. The wilderness, he said from early on in his campaign, could in fact prove a fertile ground for reinvention. “There is an opportunity to redefine the Democratic Party,” Talarico told me. “And you can’t do that if the brand is super set, or if there’s a strong leader at the top of the party.” This was a little over a year ago, and we were sitting in the lobby bar of an Arlington, Texas, hotel. “The wilderness,” Talarico continued, “is where new ideas and new leaders and new movements come forth.” At the time, I was inclined to dismiss this as a rationalization from another one of those fool’s-gold Democratic hopefuls in Texas. In retrospect, maybe Talarico was onto something. If nothing else, the Democrats’ midterm rout of Trump and his supine coalition of Republicans would seem to put to rest, at least for now, the long-running discussion of Democrats as a party out of touch, ill-defined, lacking in purpose, and perpetually ambling in this “wilderness.” I admit that I participated in a fair amount in this Democratic-doldrums discourse myself, including in an opus about the party adrift that ran in February, which now feels like a decade ago. I stand by that story. It was true then, and had been for nearly four years, if you start the clock with the 2022 midterms and the disastrous denouement of the Biden years. [ Read: Democrats will likely disappoint voters soon ] The sheer magnitude of Tuesday’s drubbing of Republicans should provide an antidote to the wallowing that Democrats can be prone to. It’s impossible not to see the geographic reach of their victories, the generational ascent of so many potential stars, and the stunning margins that Democrats ran up across the country and not conclude that the party has legitimate reason to feel good about itself. This was a bona fide “thumpin,’” as another unpopular Republican president, George W. Bush, called his own midterm debacle 20 years ago. The requisite chest-thumpin’ from Democrats commenced immediately on Tuesday night. “We have five words for the American people,” Chuck Schumer, the likely next Senate majority leader, proclaimed to reporters as the returns poured in. “Relief is on the way.” Here are five more words for Democrats to keep in mind: Enjoy this while it lasts. The “what next” of this discussion is now at hand. And it’s pretty clear that Democrats should avoid the obvious trap of thinking that their victory means they’ve magically solved their “brand problem,” “trust problem,” or “working-class-voter problem,” among various others . The initial sense of punch-drunk euphoria will yield to questions about what the party’s sprawling new legislative majorities should focus on, how they should engage (if at all) with Trump and Republicans, what ideological framework (progressive versus moderate) they should embrace, and who should lead them going into 2028. Political victory laps can be fun but fleeting, especially for governing tribes famously given to angst and discord. Inevitably, the second-guessing and hand-wringing will return, and probably soon. In politics, the simplest explanation for an election result is usually the smartest one (and less time-consuming than reading those endless postmortems). Tuesday’s result can be overwhelmingly ascribed to a repudiation of Trump, rather than revealing anything definitive about the diverse assortment of Democrats who prevailed. The political analyst Charlie Cook, of The Cook Political Report, gave preliminary voice to this notion when he predicted in September that this midterm would represent a “red undertow” rather than a blue wave. The results would be driven more by revulsion toward Trump and his various legislative lickspittles than by any dramatic reinvention by Democrats—or by some sudden mass affection for them by the electorate. This was rendered vividly in an NBC News poll released just before the election, in which voters declared themselves just not that into Democrats, despite their massive advantages leading into Election Day. Only 29 percent of respondents said that they viewed the party favorably, while 38 percent viewed Republicans positively. About half of the people surveyed said that they held a negative view of both parties. Trump will be around as the Democrats’ go-to foil for only so much longer. He has been a turnout machine for them as well as for Republicans. He has defined the GOP for the past decade, and has also defined the Democrats in opposition. It is not hard to imagine that a Republican president who did not, say, capriciously impose tariffs, start unpopular wars, or talk incessantly about building a White House ballroom would have had a considerably better midterm experience than Trump and the GOP just did. And far fewer Americans would have ever heard of Senators-Elect Talarico, Annie Andrews (South Carolina), or Adam Hamilton (Kansas). What should also be clear to Democrats is that their time is limited. Again and again, voters have shown punishing impatience with parties that don’t deliver for them quickly, especially on such close-to-the-bone economic issues as inflation. Americans have not hesitated to swing back and forth between the two parties. When was the last election, anyway, in which voters have not been described as “angry,” “frustrated,” or “fed-up?” [ Read: ‘We did this for this man?’ ] In the short term, at least, Democrats can break out their Nutter Butters and enjoy the crack-up on the other side, where the center of political drama and division in America has shifted decisively since Tuesday. House Speaker Mike Johnson said that he won’t run for minority leader, setting up a potentially bitter race to succeed him; Vice President Vance blamed Tuesday’s pummeling on the Iran war (wait, whose idea was that?); and Trump chalked up the defeat to not being on the ballot himself (effectively blaming Republicans who were). Democrats suddenly have real leverage in Washington. Trump is, to say the least, not easily humbled and not much for self-examination or course correction (to wit, he spent part of yesterday showing off his in-progress White House ballroom). He is, however, a survivor, and will take what lifelines are available. Lo and behold: “I have a lot of friends who are Democrats, believe it or not,” Trump said on Fox. “I’ve already spoken to some of them,” he added. Presumably, one of these people was Schumer , who indicated Tuesday that he would be open to working with Trump, so long as he “will actually change his ways.” It certainly beats the wilderness. Yesterday, I reached out to Democratic National Committee chair Ken Martin, whose arrival in Washington last year was marked by infighting at the DNC, a fundraising drought, and unflattering stories about him in the press—my own among them. I’d made him the hapless head of Democratic doom in my article in February, characterizing the chairman’s demeanor as one of “resting dread face,” a description that he presumably did not appreciate. So after the election, I invited him to take an oratorical victory lap on my head. He demurred, except for this brief “update” from DNC Communications Director Rosemary Boeglin, via text: “Ken Martin has turned the frown upside down on his resting dread face.”

items.title: Fanzone sport inclusive au jardin public Rufisque : briser les codes et changer le regard sur le handicap
items.description: Passer par le parasport pour sortir des clichés, rompre avec l’exclusion et offrir l’épanouissement à tous les jeunes : telle est la finalité recherchée à travers cette journée de sensibilisation, associée à une fête foraine, organisée par l’Association sport pour tous (Ast) au Jardin public de Rufisque, dans la dynamique des Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse. Des centaines d’enfants valides comme en situation de handicap ont participé ensemble, ce matin, au Jardin public de Rufisque, dans un esprit festif, à plusieurs activités parasportives comme le cécifoot, le basket en fauteuil roulant ainsi que des jeux d’olympiades. Cette activité de sensibilisation, menée par l’Association sport pour tous (Ast) dans la dynamique des JOJ, vise à matérialiser concrètement l’inclusion. « Avant, les enfants étaient séparés, mais nous avons voulu donner tout son sens au terme d’inclusivité par la pratique. C’est ce qui nous a amenés à organiser des compétitions réunissant les enfants valides et ceux en situation de handicap », explique Fatou Thioune, présidente de l’Ast. Selon elle, ladite association qu’elle dirige a été créée pour faire sauter les barrières et réduire les disparités entre les « valides » et les « invalides ». Partenaire stratégique du Conseil départemental de Rufisque dans le cadre de ce projet entamé depuis 2024, le Conseil régional d’Île-de-France réaffirme son implication sur la question du sport inclusif. Selon Frédéric Lagrand, chargé de la coopération, le sport doit être accessible à tous et à toutes. A lire aussi : L’engagement pour le bien-être de sa communauté « Nous essayons de faire le pont entre la mobilisation qui a eu lieu pendant les Jeux de Paris en 2024 et celle prévue pendant les Jeux de Dakar en 2026. Le sport est important pour la santé physique et la santé mentale de chacun », estime-t-il. D’ailleurs, il constate que les enfants n’ont pas mis beaucoup de temps à se détendre et à s’amuser ensemble. Lagrand en a profité pour inviter à briser les barrières, à sortir des clichés et à changer de regard sur le handicap. Plusieurs moyens, souligne-t-il, ont été mis en avant pour parvenir à davantage d’inclusion : la formation des coachs, des élus et des journalistes sur le parasport ; l’organisation de colloques ; l’organisation de journées de sensibilisation du grand public, etc. L’association ainsi que ses partenaires souhaitent que la dynamique autour du parasport se poursuive au Sénégal jusqu’aux Jeux de la Francophonie, prévus à Dakar. « Il y a quelques épreuves parasportives aux Jeux de la Francophonie, mais pas beaucoup. On pourrait donc se mobiliser pour qu’il y en ait davantage et que le parasport y occupe une vraie place », tout en regrettant son absence aux Joj. La cérémonie a été parrainée par Moussa Samb, président de l’Association départementale des amis et parents d’enfants inadaptés. Il s’est réjoui de cette belle initiative visant à promouvoir l’inclusion des personnes vivant avec un handicap. Mohamed DIENE (Correspondant)

items.title: FG to deploy mobile CNG stations for rural communities
items.description: By Johnbosco Agbakwuru The Federal Government is exploring the use of mobile Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) refuelling stations to improve gas availability in rural areas, especially for farmers who need more affordable energy for irrigation and agricultural production. The disclosure was made by Ismaeel Ahmed, Chairman/CEO of the Presidential CNG Initiative and Electric Vehicles (Pi-CNG & EV), at the APC–Progressive Strategy Roundtable event in Abuja, themed Promise to Proof: The Renewed Hope Conversation Speaking at the session, “Fuel That Works: Reliable Energy, Affordable Transport and Fair Prices for Every Household and Business,” Ahmed said the government was considering mobile CNG stations to bring fuel to remote communities, where permanent facilities may not be commercially attractive to private investors. He explained that consultations with state governments, particularly in northern Nigeria, had revealed that the demand for CNG was increasingly extending beyond transportation to agricultural activities. He said farmers are seeking to switch from expensive diesel and petrol to CNG-powered irrigation pumps to reduce production costs. Ahmed, the Convener of the Roundtable, cited Jigawa State as an example, noting that the governor had told the initiative that more than two million farmers in the state could benefit from affordable energy for irrigation He explained that mechanical irrigation pumps could cover about three hectares of farmland, compared with solar-powered pumps, which typically cover about one hectare. He said although solar-powered irrigation had been introduced as an alternative, some farmers preferred mechanical pumps because of their greater coverage and operational capacity. Ahmed said the Federal Government was committed to aggressively pursuing the expansion of gas infrastructure, adding that President Bola Tinubu had given the initiative the go-ahead to intensify its activities. However, he identified gas supply and delays in obtaining licences for CNG refuelling stations as major challenges that needed to be addressed. He appealed to the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority (NMDPRA) to help accelerate the licensing process for investors seeking to establish CNG stations. He acknowledged the importance of safety regulations, explaining that gas infrastructure required strict safety considerations, but urged the regulator to find ways of expediting the process in view of the urgency of the programme. He also raised the possibility of deploying mobile CNG stations to serve farmers and other users in remote communities where investors might not immediately find it economically viable to establish permanent facilities. Ahmed said the CNG programme had recorded about 143,000 vehicle conversions, with investments estimated at $2.6 billion. The roundtable also featured presentations by the Managing Director of the Rural Electrification Agency, Dr. Abba Abubakar Aliyu; the representative of the Niger Delta Power Holding Company, Mr. Abdullahi Kassim; the Chairman of the Nigerian Electricity Regulatory Commission, Dr. Musiliu Oseni; and the representative of the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority, Dr. Mustapha Lamorde. On rural electrification, Aliyu discussed electricity-access gaps, national mapping, least-cost electrification planning and the deployment of mini-grids and captive power projects. The meeting was informed of plans to deploy 1,350 mini-grids under a $750 million project to improve electricity access in underserved communities. Kassim, while presenting the activities of the Niger Delta Power Holding Company, discussed the company’s ownership structure, the history of the National Integrated Power Projects assets and its contribution to electricity generation. He disclosed that the company operates 10 power plants with a combined generation capacity of 4,000 megawatts. He also highlighted the company’s transmission and distribution infrastructure, industrial power initiatives, solar deployments and recently awarded community infrastructure contracts. Oseni addressed electricity tariffs, affordability and service delivery, explaining the different customer bands and the relationship between electricity tariffs and hours of supply. He said electricity costs were estimated at about ₦200 per kilowatt-hour, while the commission was pursuing measures to improve power supply through investments in generation, mini-grids, debt recovery and net billing. NERC also reported an increase of approximately 780 megawatts in installed generation capacity. On fuel availability and energy security, Lamorde discussed the regulatory framework for petroleum supply, domestic refining, product pricing and strategic fuel reserves. The presentation highlighted efforts to monitor fuel availability, with a target of 30 days of supply monitoring and an eventual goal of building strategic reserves capable of covering 90 days. The meeting was also informed that the Port Harcourt, Warri and Kaduna refineries, with a combined capacity of about 445,000 barrels per day, were currently shut down. The representative said the government was engaging international technical expertise to facilitate the resolution of challenges affecting the facilities. He further disclosed that more than 26 refineries had been licensed across the country, while a pre-start-up safety review had recently been conducted for a 30,000-barrel-per-day Brenco refinery, which is expected to commence operations soon. The discussion also addressed product quality, with the petroleum regulator highlighting the modernisation of laboratories across the country. Two laboratories had recently been completed, while another was expected to be commissioned before the end of the year. Participants raised questions about historical electricity generation capacity, additional refinery investments, local production of electric vehicles and solar panels, diaspora investment opportunities and complaints against electricity distribution companies. On electric vehicles and battery production, Ahmed said lithium development was being handled by the Ministry of Solid Minerals Development, adding that the government was interested in encouraging local battery manufacturing, vehicle assembly and the production of electric vehicles. Responding to concerns about electricity disconnections, Oseni explained that mass disconnections were prohibited and outlined complaint channels available to electricity consumers. He also discussed possible compensation arrangements for customers who finance improvements to electricity distribution networks. The NERC chairman acknowledged that electricity supply to Band A customers had improved but admitted that overall service delivery remained below the desired level. items.title: De « Magic in the Air » à la Tanière : le joli destin de Pathé Mboup
items.description: Pathé Mboup change de scène. Il y a douze ans, il apparaissait dans un clip qui allait faire danser des millions de personnes à travers le monde. Aujourd’hui, le natif de Mbao s’apprête à vivre une tout autre aventure : sa première convocation en équipe nationale A du Sénégal. L’attaquant du Stade Brestois fait partie des nouveaux joueurs retenus par Patrick Vieira pour la double confrontation contre le Soudan, dans le cadre des éliminatoires de la CAN 2027. L’anecdote a de quoi surprendre. Selon RMC Sport, le jeune Pathé Mboup figurait, à seulement 11 ans, dans le clip de « Magic in the Air », le célèbre titre du groupe ivoirien Magic System. Il y incarnait un jeune footballeur portant un maillot jaune. Une apparition qui prend aujourd’hui une dimension particulière, alors que le garçon du clip vient de franchir une étape importante dans sa carrière en rejoignant la sélection des Lions. Sorti en 2014, « Magic in the Air » est bien plus qu’un morceau festif. Portée par un refrain entraînant et des sonorités dansantes, la chanson célèbre le football, la fête et l’ambiance populaire autour du ballon rond. Le titre, enregistré par Magic System avec le chanteur marocain Chawki, s’est rapidement imposé comme un hymne des stades. Il a notamment accompagné les succès de l’équipe de France, qui se l’est approprié lors de l’Euro 2016 puis de la Coupe du monde 2018. Le clip officiel dépasse aujourd’hui les 564 millions de vues sur YouTube. Brest, le tremplin vers les Lions Douze ans après cette apparition, Pathé Mboup poursuit son chemin dans le football professionnel. Formé à l’AS Dakar Sacré-Cœur, où il est arrivé à l’âge de 10 ans, le joueur a ensuite connu plusieurs expériences en Europe, notamment à Molenbeek et au Pau FC, avant de rejoindre le Stade Brestois. À 23 ans, il s’est installé dans le paysage de la Ligue 1 française. Son début de saison avec Brest est marqué par deux buts et une passe décisive en neuf rencontres de championnat. Des performances qui ont retenu l’attention de Patrick Vieira, désireux d’élargir ses options offensives et d’évaluer de nouveaux profils. Cette première convocation ouvre ainsi un nouveau chapitre pour le jeune attaquant. De l’enfant qui faisait quelques apparitions dans un clip tourné au Sénégal à l’international appelé à défendre les couleurs nationales, le parcours de Pathé Mboup offre une belle histoire. La magie de « Magic in the Air » appartient désormais aux souvenirs ; celle de la Tanière reste à écrire. Cheikh Gora DIOP

items.title: Ogun ready for State Police – Abiodun
items.description: By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta Ogun State Governor, Dapo Abiodun has declared his administration’s readiness to establish a state police force, describing it as a critical step towards strengthening security, protecting investments and sustaining the state’s growing economic activities. The governor also announced the immediate commencement of a social investment cash transfer programme for vulnerable residents to cushion the effects of rising food and transportation costs. Abiodun made the announcements at a town hall meeting on the 2027 budget and the 2027–2029 Medium Term Expenditure Framework (MTEF) for Remo Division, held at the Akarigbo Palace, Sagamu. Speaking on the proposed establishment of state police, the governor, who chairs the Nigeria Governors’ Forum Committee on State Police, said Ogun was prepared to embrace the initiative, noting that the state’s expanding industrial and commercial activities required a more robust security framework. He declared: “I am the Chairman of the Governors’ Forum on State Police creation. Ogun State is ready for state police.” Abiodun said his administration had consistently strengthened the state’s security architecture through the provision of operational vehicles, allowances and equipment, as well as increased recruitment into the Ogun State Security Network, popularly known as Amotekun. He disclosed that Amotekun and the So-Safe Corps currently had a combined strength of about 6,000 personnel. “To protect the gains we have made, we have continued to strengthen our security architecture by providing them with vehicles, allowances and equipment. We have empowered our Amotekun and increased their recruitment,” he said. On the cash transfer initiative, the governor said the programme was designed to provide direct financial support to vulnerable households grappling with the rising cost of living, particularly food and transportation. He linked the prevailing economic pressures partly to disruptions in the global oil and gas supply chain arising from the ongoing Israel-American-Iran conflict, which he said had contributed to rising oil prices and transportation costs. “We are going to start the implementation of our social investment cash initiative. We are going to transfer cash to our people to cushion the effects of this America-Israel-Iran war,” he stated. The governor disclosed that the programme would commence immediately in Sagamu, with beneficiaries already identified and captured in the state’s database expected to receive payment alerts. He added that the initiative would subsequently be extended to other communities across Remoland and the entire state. “I am starting that today in Sagamu. I’m going into Ogijo from here. All those who have been generated to benefit will get their alerts today while I’m there. I’m going to do the same across Remoland and of course, the whole state,” he said. Abiodun further announced plans to sink boreholes in all 236 wards across the state, while also providing transformers and solar-powered streetlights to improve access to basic amenities and enhance security in communities. He assured residents that Remoland remained central to his administration’s development agenda, stressing that the division was an active participant and beneficiary of the economic transformation taking place across Ogun. “Remoland is not on the sidelines of these developments. You are right in the middle of it. You are a participant and a contributor to this economic improvement,” he said. Earlier, the Economic Adviser to the Governor and Commissioner for Finance, Mr Dapo Okubadejo, said effective governance depended on open dialogue, active citizen participation and mutual accountability between the government and the people. He noted that the performance of any administration should ultimately be assessed by the tangible improvements its policies and programmes brought to the lives of citizens, particularly through infrastructure development and social interventions. Providing an overview of the state’s fiscal performance, Okubadejo disclosed that Ogun recorded an expenditure performance of N490 billion out of the N703 billion budget estimate for 2024, representing approximately 70 per cent. He said the 2025 budget of N1.05 trillion recorded expenditure of about N700 billion, representing 65 per cent performance. According to him, the 2026 budget, valued at N1.67 trillion, had continued to support government interventions in infrastructure, education, youth empowerment, agriculture and other critical sectors. “As we commence preparation for the 2027 budget within the 2027–2029 Medium Term Expenditure Framework, this town hall meeting provides the opportunity to share the policies, programmes and projects that would be embarked upon next year,” he said. Speaking on behalf of the chairmen of Sagamu, Remo North and Ikenne Local Government Areas, the Chairman of Sagamu Local Government, Afolabi Odulate, appealed to the state government to address what he described as the encroachment of Lagos into Ogun through border communities. He also called for the rehabilitation of deteriorating roads across the three local government areas to facilitate movement, stimulate commercial activities and improve the living conditions of residents. The Akarigbo of Remoland, Oba Babatunde Ajayi, commended the state government for the development projects executed across the division but called for the establishment of a monitoring team to ensure that public facilities were properly utilised and maintained. The monarch also appealed for the establishment of federal tertiary institutions in Remoland and urged the state government to ensure that indigenes of the division were adequately included in the state’s economic development initiatives. Similarly, the Chairman of the Remo Division of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Nigeria (ICAN), Chief Adewale Kalejaye, called for stronger collaboration between the professional body and the state government to broaden the tax base and improve revenue generation. He also advocated increased funding for Sustainable Development Goals initiatives, particularly programmes targeted at reducing poverty and hunger and improving access to education for children. items.title: Surcharge des poids lourds : des amendes pouvant atteindre 100 000 DA
items.description: La Gendarmerie nationale a entamé une vaste campagne de sensibilisation aux dangers de la surcharge des véhicules lourds sur les routes algériennes. Les conducteurs des poids lourds ayant dépassé la charge autorisée risquent de payer de lourdes amendes. Une surcharge de moins de 10 % est passible d’une amende de 7 000 dinars contre 8 000 dinars pour les surcharges qui se situent entre 10 % et 20 % du poids autorisé, a annoncé la Gendarmerie nationale sur sa page Facebook – Tariki. Des camions avec une surcharge de 80 % L’amende passe à 9 000 dinars pour les dépassements de charge établis entre 20 % et 30 % du poids légal. Au-delà de 30 %, la contravention devient un délit passible d’une amende allant de 70 000 à 100 000 dinars, a averti la même source. La gendarmerie a indiqué que ses services ont enregistré des surcharges qui ont dépassé 80 % du poids légal, rappelant que ce comportement rend le véhicule plus difficile à contrôler et augmente les risques d’accidents de la route. « Le respect des charges légales est un acte de prévention qui protège des vies et assure la sécurité de tous », a-t-on souligné. Des stations mobiles de pesage des poids lourds Les unités de la gendarmerie ont été équipées de stations mobiles de pesage destinées à contrôler la charge des véhicules poids lourds, à la suite d’une convention signée, en juillet dernier, avec le ministère des Travaux publics. La convention a pour objectif de protéger les infrastructures routières et de réduire les accidents de la circulation. Le ministre des Travaux publics, Abdelkader Djellaoui, a affirmé, lors de la signature de la convention, que « la surcharge constitue l'une des principales causes de la dégradation des routes, des ponts et des ouvrages d'art, réduisant leur durée de vie, outre sa contribution à la survenue d'accidents de la circulation entraînant des pertes humaines et matérielles ».
