items.title: UCAES SRC president urges young people to embrace agriculture
items.description: The newly elected President of the Students’ Representative Council (SRC) of the University College of Agriculture and Environmental Studies (UCAES), Prince Amoako Atta, has called for increased youth participation in agriculture and environmental protection. The 18th SRC President expressed concern over the declining interest in agriculture, despite the sector employing more than 40 per cent of Ghana’s population. He attributed the trend partly to illegal mining, popularly known as galamsey, deforestation and the perception among young people that farming is unattractive. According to him, Ghana’s development prospects are closely linked to its ability to strengthen agricultural production and protect the environment. Using California as an example, Hon. Amoako Atta highlighted the economic benefits of investing in agriculture, noting that communities could achieve significant growth when the sector receives adequate attention, resources and technological support. “Agriculture has evolved beyond the traditional use of cutlasses and hoes, with emerging opportunities in agribusiness, biotechnology and other technology-driven agricultural practices,” he said. He therefore urged young people to change their perception of farming and explore the numerous opportunities available across the agricultural value chain. Hon. Amoako Atta also emphasised the importance of environmental protection, arguing that human survival depends largely on maintaining a healthy and sustainable environment. He consequently called on individuals, institutions and the government to make agriculture and environmental protection national priorities to safeguard the country’s future. The UCAES SRC President further appealed to the government to extend support to private institutions specialising in agricultural and environmental education, stressing that their contributions to national development should not be overlooked because of their ownership status. “The government must therefore pay attention to and support institutions that focus on agriculture and environmental studies to help make Ghana a major food hub,” he said. He maintained that supporting such institutions would strengthen agricultural education, encourage innovation and equip more young people with the knowledge and skills needed to transform the sector. Mr. Amoako Atta added that prioritising agriculture would not only improve food security but also promote peace, protect the ecosystem and create a sustainable environment for present and future generations. He reiterated that a renewed national commitment to agriculture and environmental protection was essential to building a stronger and more resilient economy.

items.title: Official says 273 arrested in NCCIA raid on 'illegal' call centre on Karachi's Sharea Faisal
items.description: KARACHI: The National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) on Thursday claimed to have conducted a major operation against an alleged international fraud network and arrested 273 people from a call centre located on Sharea Faisal. Addressing a press conference in Karachi, NCCIA Additional Director Shahzad Akbar said 339 laptops, 152 cell phones and four computers were seized during the operation. “The NCCIA conducted a major enforcement operation on Nov 4 at a premises located near Kavish Crown Plaza in connection with an ongoing enquiry into an alleged international financial fraud network and call centre,” he said. During the operation, the investigating team identified a call centre operating under the name Voxtron Solutions. According to preliminary findings, it was allegedly involved in fraudulent activities targeting foreign nationals through impersonation, identity misuse and caller ID spoofing, he said. According to Akbar, initial investigations indicated that the facility was allegedly operating under the pretext of providing debt validation services. “Personnel associated with the operation reportedly impersonated representatives of foreign banking institutions and debt validation service providers, contacting individuals abroad and offering assistance in the verification and validation of their outstanding financial obligations,” he stated. The NCCIA official said investigators had established “reasonable grounds” to suspect that the alleged scheme was designed to induce victims into disclosing sensitive personal and financial information, including Social Security Numbers and payment card credentials. He said preliminary findings further suggested that the information obtained was subsequently exploited to facilitate unauthorised financial transactions through merchant accounts. The proceeds generated through these transactions were reportedly transferred to Pakistan through company accounts and remittance channels, indicating possible cross-border movement of illicit funds, he said. Akbar said all recovered evidence and material was taken into official custody and referred for detailed technical examination and digital forensic analysis. Akbar said 273 suspects were arrested for further investigation and proceedings and a case was registered under Sections 3 (unauthorised access to information system or data), 4 (unauthorised copying or transmission of data), 13 (electronic forgery), 14 (electronic fraud), 16 (unauthorised use of identity information) and 26 (spoofing) of the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act, 2016 (Peca). Families stage protest Meanwhile, the suspects’ relatives and local residents staged a protest against the raid and arrests near the Baloch Colony Bridge on Sharea Faisal, disrupting the smooth flow of traffic along Karachi’s main artery. The demonstrators protested the arrest of around 100 women from the call centre, claiming that their children worked there and had no involvement in illegal activities, demanding the suspects’ immediate release. A traffic police spokesperson said that because of the protest, traffic was diverted on alternative routes. Local police and traffic officials held talks with the protesters and persuaded them to disperse. Traffic flow was restored on the main road by 1:22pm. Last week, the agency claimed to have arrested over 40 suspects during a raid on an “illegal call centre” located on Sharea Faisal. An NCCIA spokesperson alleged that the call centre was involved in fraud against foreigners.

items.title: Atiku, Obi, SDP, CUPP, ADC kick as court sacks Mark-led ADC exco
items.description: By Nwafor Sunday, Henry Umoru, Ikechukwu Nnochiri, Luminous Jannamike, & John Alechelu The Federal High Court in Abuja’s decision to sack the Senator David Mark-led executive committee of the African Democratic Congress, ADC, and nullify all actions taken by it has drawn criticism from former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar; Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, presidential candidate Peter Obi; the Social Democratic Party, SDP, and the Coalition of United Political Parties, CUPP. While Atiku accused the ruling All Progressives Congress, APC, of using the judgment to frustrate his presidential ambition and weaken his support base in the North, Obi urged Nigerians and the judiciary to protect democratic principles and allow opposition parties to thrive. The court, in a judgment delivered on Thursday by Justice Peter Lifu , declared the Mark-led ADC caretaker committee illegal and invalidated all actions taken by it, including the party’s presidential primary that produced Atiku as its candidate for the 2027 general election. The judgment followed a suit instituted by Nafiu Bala Gombe, a former National Deputy Chairman of the ADC (North-East), who challenged the process through which the Mark-led leadership assumed control of the party. Gombe had argued that following the resignation of the party’s former National Chairman, Ralph Nwosu, he was entitled to assume the leadership of the party. The court upheld his claims and granted the reliefs sought. The ruling has raised questions about the status of Atiku’s candidacy, coming barely 24 hours after he held a campaign rally in Sokoto State. Atiku alleges plot to weaken Northern support Reacting to the judgment, Atiku accused the APC of using the court ruling to frustrate his presidential ambition and contain the ADC’s growing political influence ahead of the 2027 elections. Atiku said the ruling came barely 24 hours after thousands of supporters welcomed him to Sokoto for the launch of the ADC campaign, alleging that the development was part of a strategy to weaken his Northern support base and halt the spread of his campaign beyond the region. In a statement issued on Thursday by Phrank Shaibu, Director of Strategic Communication of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, the former Vice-President insisted that the judgment would neither derail the party’s campaign nor diminish its appeal across the country. He said the reception in Sokoto reflected Nigerians’ growing frustration with economic hardship and their desire for a change of government. “The people of Sokoto came out in their thousands because they are hungry for change and believe in our promise to make life affordable again. What we witnessed in Sokoto is only the beginning. The people of Kebbi will have their say, and so will Nigerians across the country as our campaign moves forward,” he said. Rejecting attempts to portray his candidacy as a Northern project, Atiku said the economic crisis confronting Nigerians had made his political message relevant across regional boundaries. “My roots are in Northern Nigeria, but my candidacy belongs to all Nigerians. There is a difference between being from the North and being a candidate only for the North. Hunger and hardship do not respect regional boundaries. Nigerians across the country are suffering under this government, and they deserve a leader with a credible plan to make life affordable again,” he said. Atiku alleged that the judgment was intended to disrupt the momentum of his campaign and weaken the opposition’s growing political reach. “The timing of this judgment is no coincidence. It is part of a strategy to weaken my support in the North and frustrate a campaign whose message is resonating across the country. But the ruling party’s greatest miscalculation is to assume that my support ends in the North. What we saw in Sokoto, what we will see in Kebbi and across the country, is the strength of a national movement,” he said. On the legal implications, Atiku questioned why the leadership dispute was reopened despite an earlier judgment by Justice Musa Liman of the Federal High Court, Abuja, in Suit No. FHC/ABJ/CS/1637/2025. He said the court had dismissed the challenge to the David Mark-led leadership after upholding objections bordering on jurisdiction, standing and failure to exhaust internal party remedies, adding that the substantive issues were also resolved in favour of the defendants. “Why, after that judgment, was another case filed to reopen the same dispute? This is a calculated attempt to circumvent a subsisting judgment. We will challenge this judicial manoeuvre at the Court of Appeal,” he said. The former Vice-President urged ADC supporters to remain peaceful and law-abiding, insisting that the ruling would not interrupt the party’s mobilisation. “Our journey to rescue Nigeria from the hardship imposed by the APC government is a long one. Our Affordable Life campaign will continue because Nigerians deserve relief from this crushing cost-of-living crisis,” he said. With the campaign train already in Kebbi, Atiku urged supporters to take the party’s message from house to house and door to door, declaring, “There is no shaking.” Obi warns against undermining democracy Also reacting to the development, Obi urged Nigerians and the judiciary to protect democratic principles and allow opposition parties to thrive. Obi, who expressed shock over the judgment, said the development had created uncertainty in the country’s political landscape, particularly with the 2027 general election approaching. He disclosed this in a statement posted on his X platform on Thursday. The former Anambra State governor said although he respected the court’s authority to determine disputes in accordance with the law, the timing of the judgment raised concerns about electoral certainty. “I do not challenge the ruling of the court. The court of law is constituted to determine disputes according to the law. My concern is that three months before a general election, it is in the public interest to have certainty,” he said. Obi argued that uncertainty over political parties and their candidates close to an election could undermine the electoral process and restrict the space for opposition campaigns. He alleged that the ruling party was engineering instability within opposition parties, claiming that similar developments had affected him in the Labour Party. He also alleged that opposition campaigns had been subjected to violence, describing the developments as part of what he called efforts to shrink the civic space and weaken opposition politics. Emphasising the importance of voters in a democracy, Obi said the choice of political leaders should ultimately rest with the electorate. “One mark of democracy is that at all times, it is voters and not courts that choose leaders. I trust in the judiciary. As a public officer, I have shown deep respect for the judiciary,” he said. He appealed to the judiciary and other stakeholders to protect democratic institutions and ensure that candidates were allowed to participate freely in electoral contests. Obi further warned against weakening opposition politics, citing the spread of military rule in parts of West Africa as a reason Nigeria should strengthen its democratic institutions. According to him, the survival of democracy requires a political environment in which opposition parties are allowed to operate, organise and compete without persecution. He said he had consistently maintained that, if elected president, he would give special attention to ensuring that opposition parties remained stable and viable. Obi added that his administration would protect opposition candidates from being pushed out of electoral contests. “This is a time to strengthen our democracy by allowing the opposition to thrive,” he said. CUPP accuses APC of pursuing one-party state Similarly, the Coalition of United Political Parties (CUPP) criticised the judgment, alleging that it could weaken opposition parties and undermine political competition in the country. In a statement issued in Abuja on Thursday through its Office of the Spokesperson, the coalition accused the ruling APC of benefiting from what it described as a systematic effort to weaken opposition parties. CUPP alleged that the judgment was part of a broader attempt to undermine opposition political structures and create conditions for a one-party state. The coalition also expressed concern over the role of the judiciary, arguing that the ruling raised questions about the courts’ responsibility to protect democratic rights and political participation. “CUPP views this controversial judgment not as an isolated legal dispute, but as part of a well-choreographed, state-sponsored onslaught aimed at wiping out viable opposition parties and turning Nigeria into a one-party state,” the statement read. It further alleged that sections of the judiciary had failed to adequately protect the interests of citizens and the electoral process. CUPP also accused the APC-led government of relying on legal technicalities to challenge opposition candidates and party leadership structures, saying such developments could restrict political competition and undermine public confidence in the electoral system. “The judiciary must remember that its allegiance belongs to the Constitution and the Nigerian people, not to the political actors of the day. When the courts become a tool for political liquidation, the very survival of our democracy is at stake,” the statement added. The coalition declared solidarity with the ADC and other opposition groups, saying it would continue to defend democratic participation and political pluralism. SDP condemns alleged move to disqualify Atiku Meanwhile, the Social Democratic Party (SDP) condemned alleged attempts to disqualify Atiku from the 2027 presidential election, insisting that political parties should be allowed to freely present candidates. The SDP National Chairman, Prof. Sadiq Gombe, stated this on Thursday in Abuja while addressing journalists after a meeting with the party’s nine governorship candidates from different states. Gombe called on the judiciary, security agencies and the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to remain impartial and protect the country’s democratic process. He also accused the APC of allegedly plotting to infiltrate opposition parties and weaken their ranks ahead of the elections. The SDP chairman alleged that the ruling party, having lost the confidence of Nigerians over its governance record, was using the proposed Rainbow Coalition to woo opposition members and undermine their unity. He, however, said the SDP was working with other opposition parties towards building a coalition of Nigerians committed to credible elections, including joint training of party agents and the establishment of common situation rooms to protect votes at polling units. Gombe reaffirmed the party’s commitment to presenting what he described as credible alternatives to Nigerians, naming its presidential candidate, Prince Adewole Adebayo, and vice-presidential candidate, Prof. Usman Bugaje. “I want to assure you that SDP, as a political party, has nothing to do with anything called Rainbow Coalition. “We are with other political parties in the opposition, doing everything possible to rescue our dear country through a coalition of the Nigerian people. “We are not into any Rainbow Coalition where we will have candidates here and profess support for the APC presidency. We are SDP and we are for SDP candidates,” he said. He said the party had resolved to discipline any member who participated in the proposed arrangement without its authorisation. The SDP chairman also expressed concern over the alleged failure of INEC to publish the names of some of the party’s candidates, saying the matter was already before the court. He accused the commission of failing to recognise the candidates despite what he described as the party’s compliance with the Electoral Act, the Constitution and its internal nomination procedures. Gombe further raised concerns about the voters’ register and the creation of polling units, warning against actions capable of undermining public confidence in the electoral process. SDP candidates strategise ahead of 2027 Earlier, the Chairman of the SDP Governors’ Forum and Nasarawa governorship candidate, Mohammed Abubakar Adamu, said the meeting was aimed at developing strategies to secure victory in the presidential, governorship and legislative elections. Adamu said the candidates shared experiences from their respective states and discussed ways to address organisational gaps ahead of the polls. The meeting brought together the party’s nine governorship candidates and members of its National Working Committee as part of efforts to strengthen its structures ahead of the 2027 general elections. ADC vows to appeal judgment The ADC has vowed to appeal the judgment. Its National Welfare Secretary, Nkemakolam Ukandu, who was joined as an interested party in the case, said the party would challenge the verdict at the appellate court. items.title: Conseil des Ministres : Assainissement du Secteur minier artisanal et création d’une société d’État « Faso SANU » ; Adoption d’un projet de loi pour le développement des activités sportives ; Création de l’Agence burkinabè de médecine traditionnelle
items.description: Le Président du Faso, Chef de l’État, le Camarade Capitaine Ibrahim TRAORÉ, a présidé, ce jeudi 5 novembre 2026, l’hebdomadaire Conseil des ministres. Cette session ordinaire a examiné et adopté plusieurs dossiers et pris d’importantes décisions pour la bonne marche de la Nation, conformément à la vision de la Révolution Progressiste Populaire (RPP) selon le Porte-parole du Gouvernement, Camarade Gilbert OUÉDRAOGO. Pour le Porte-parole du Gouvernement, Camarade Gilbert OUÉDRAOGO, les décisions ont été prises pour la bonne marche de la Nation, conformément à la vision de la Révolution Progressiste Populaire Au titre du ministère de l’Énergie, des Mines et des Carrières, le Conseil a adopté trois décrets. Le premier décret portant conditions et modalités de réorganisation de l’exploitation des sites miniers illégaux, des sites miniers illégaux faisant l’objet de conflits et des sites miniers illégaux présentant un caractère stratégique pour l’État. Selon le Ministre de l‘Énergie, des Mines et des Carrières, Camarade Yacouba Zabré GOUBA, l’adoption de ce décret vise une meilleure réorganisation de ces sites afin d’instaurer un climat apaisé pour l’exploitation artisanale de l’or. Et conformément au code minier en vigueur dans notre pays, « tout acteur qui se rendra coupable de l’emploi des enfants sur les sites miniers se verra appliqué toute la rigueur de la loi », soutient le camarade GOUBA. Selon le ministre de l'Énergie, des Mines et des Carrières, Camarade Yacouba Zabré GOUBA, « Faso Sanu » est un bras technique fort pour assainir et encadrer le sous-secteur de l'artisanat minier tout en appliquant la rigueur de la loi contre l’emploi des enfants Le deuxième décret adopté au titre du ministère en charge des mines est relatif à la création d’une société d’État dénommée Faso SANU (or, en langue dioula). Il s’agira, à travers la création de cette société, de permettre à l’État d’assurer une meilleure réorganisation du sous-secteur et de disposer d’un bras technique à même de pouvoir concourir à la prise en charge du premier décret. Selon le camarade GOUBA, Faso SANU sera détenue à 50% par la Société nationale des substances précieuses (SONASP) et 50% par le Trésor public. Quant au troisième décret, il est relatif à l’adoption des statuts de ladite société. Restructuration territoriale et opérationnelle du ministère de la santé Au titre du ministère de la Santé, le Conseil a adopté un décret modifiant l'organigramme du département. Aligné sur le nouveau découpage territorial et la mise en place des Centres médicaux communaux (CMC), ce changement ambitionne, selon le ministre de la Santé, Camarade Robert Lucien Jean-Claude KARGOUGOU, de concrétiser plus efficacement la vision du Président du Faso en matière de santé publique. Pour le ministre de la Santé, Camarade Robert Lucien Jean-Claude KARGOUGOU, la création de l'Agence Burkinabè de Médecine Traditionnelle (ABMT) vise à valoriser le caractère hautement stratégique de la médecine traditionnelle Cette vaste réorganisation s'articule autour de plusieurs innovations dont la création d'un Secrétariat général adjoint pour superviser les structures hospitalières et sociétés d'État, la mise en place de structures spécialisées que sont le Secrétariat permanent du Conseil national de lutte contre le Sida, les IST, les hépatites virales et la tuberculose, ainsi que le Secrétariat technique pour l'intelligence sanitaire. Il y a également la création du Faso Center for Disease Control and Prevention (Faso CDC) et de l'Agence burkinabè de médecine traditionnelle, valorisant ainsi le patrimoine médical national et le renforcement du maillage territorial avec la création de directions provinciales de la Santé et de centres hospitaliers provinciaux. Dans un souci d'efficience et de rationalisation, le texte acte par ailleurs la dissolution de la SOGEMAB (Société de gestion d'équipements et de la maintenance biomédicale) et du secrétariat technique en charge de la multisectorialité pour la nutrition. Refonte du cadre juridique sportif Pour le compte du département en charge des sports, un projet de loi a été adopté afin de combler les lacunes de la loi 050 portant orientation du sport et des loisirs datant de 2019. Selon la ministre Annick Lydie Djouma PIKBOUGOUM/ZINGUÉ OUATTARA, cette relecture vise à « mettre en cohérence les ambitions de notre pays, définir une vision claire et un plan d'action concerté pour transformer le secteur du sport en un moteur de développement socioéconomique ». Selon la ministre des Sports, de la Jeunesse et de l'Emploi, Camarade Annick PIKBOUGOUM ZINGUÉ OUATTARA, la relecture de la Loi 050 de 2019 vise à transformer le sport en un moteur de développement socio-économique Parmi les innovations phares de ce texte figurent : la protection sociale et salariale des sportifs à travers une rémunération décente, la subordination des participations internationales des équipes nationales à une autorisation gouvernementale préalable, l'encadrement inclusif du sport pour les personnes vivant avec un handicap, le renforcement des règles relatives à la santé des athlètes et à la lutte antidopage. Direction de la communication de la Présidence du Faso

items.title: Espace jeu : Pour le bonheur des enfants
items.description: Le Salon international de l’artisanat de Ouagadougou(SIAO) fait un clin aux enfants à travers un espace de jeux. Il y a de l’engouement à l’espace de jeux dédié aux enfants situé au sein du SIAO. Tobogans, manèges (mini-carrousel, jumping-car…) jeu de réalité virtuelle, tir au but, panier à basket, trampoline, train, tri de couleur, etc. offrent du plaisir aux bambins à cette 18 ème édition du SIAO. Entre cris de joie, éclats de rires de ceux qui d’apparence savourent ce moment, les pleurs de certains qui sont pris de peur ou de panique et les plaintes de ceux qui s’impatientent dans les files d’attente, l’ambiance est électrique. Les parents, constitués majoritairement de dames participent aussi à cette atmosphère de fête en immortalisant ces instants d’enthousiasme de leurs enfants, question d’avoir un souvenir de leur passage au SIAO 2026. Les mamans immortalisent les instants de détente de leurs progénitures lors de ce SIAO 2026. « J’ai aimé ! C’était la guerre et j’étais dans l’espace en train de neutraliser les avions ennemis », s’est-exprimé Soulmeymane Coulibaly, élève en classe de 5 ème. Selon Minougou Grace Deborah, monitrice à BIBI Parc, le jeu consiste à porter un casque au joueur à travers lequel il perçoit des images qui le plongent dans un univers réel. Avec l’engouement que suscite l’espace du jeu, la monitrice a affirmé qu’ils sont préparés à cet effet. Son collège Abdallah Tiendrebeogo a confié que l’âge de participation au jeu a été revu à la hausse afin de permettre au plus grand nombre d’enfants de se faire plaisir. Kadi RABO

items.title: Opération humanitaire à Alechki : Vladimir Poutine a personnellement donné les instructions pour assurer le succès du cessez-le-feu
items.description: Une ceremonie consacree a la reussite de l'operation humanitaire menee a Alechki, pres de la ligne de front dans la region de Kherson, s'est tenue ce 5 novembre a la Maison Blanche, a l'initiative de la Premiere dame des etats-Unis, Melania Trump. Du cote russe, Kirill Dmitriev, representant special du president russe, et Iana Lantratova, mediatrice russe des droits de l'homme, y ont ete invites. Au nom de Vladimir Poutine et du peuple russe, Kirill Dmitriev a remercie Melania Trump « pour son role humanitaire eminent dans la resolution de la situation a Alechki et de ce probleme humanitaire ». « Elle a joue un role de leadership crucial dans la coordination des operations humanitaires a Alechki et la reunification des familles russes et ukrainiennes », a-t-il ajoute, soulignant que cette mission illustrait ce qu'il etait possible d'accomplir lorsque la compassion, la determination et la cooperation s'unissaient. Kirill Dmitriev a egalement indique que Vladimir Poutine avait personnellement donne les instructions necessaires a la mise en œuvre du cessez-le-feu a Alechki. Il a ajoute que le president russe appreciait particulierement les efforts de paix de son homologue americain Donald Trump et de son equipe, engages dans l'elaboration d'un plan de paix pour l'Ukraine. « La cooperation entre la Russie et les etats-Unis compte non seulement pour nos deux nations, mais aussi pour le monde entier. Continuons a apporter ensemble la plus grande contribution possible a l'humanite. Construisons un avenir de paix, de partenariat et de prosperite pour le bien de nos familles, de nos enfants et des generations futures », a declare le representant special du president russe. Melania Trump, pour sa part, a salue la cooperation entre Moscou et Kiev dans la conduite de l'operation humanitaire. Elle a egalement exprime l'espoir que cette initiative ouvre la voie a une paix plus large. « La treve a Alechki n'aurait pas ete possible sans le president Poutine et le president Zelensky. Leur cooperation etablit un precedent significatif pour faire avancer la paix dans toute la region », a souligne la Premiere dame americaine. La mission humanitaire a Alechki s'est deroulee les 30 et 31 octobre, apres l' annonce prealable d'un cessez-le-feu de part et d'autre. Iana Lantratova a affirme que l'operation s'etait deroulee sans incident et que toutes les personnes souhaitant quitter Alechki avaient pu le faire, y compris celles qui ne s'etaient pas inscrites a l'avance. La mediatrice a egalement exprime sa gratitude envers les militaires russes, qui ont assure le succes de la mission. Selon elle, Moscou et Kiev ont convenu d'organiser des missions humanitaires regulieres.

items.title: Téhéran peine à bloquer les exportations de pétrole du Golfe
items.description: Malgré la pression exercée par les Gardiens de la révolution islamique, les flux pétroliers en provenance des principaux producteurs arabes du Golfe ont retrouvé en octobre un niveau proche de celui d’avant-guerre. L’Arabie saoudite et le Koweït ont ainsi exporté plus de 99 % des volumes de brut qu’ils expédiaient avant le conflit, malgré les attaques de Téhéran. En effet, l’Iran a multiplié les frappes ces dernières semaines : en octobre, 35 navires ont été attaqués selon l’UKMTO, plus qu’au cours de n’importe quel mois depuis le début de la guerre. Hier, mercredi 4 novembre, les Gardiens de la révolution ont affirmé que quatre pétroliers avaient été détruits au sud du détroit d’Ormuz après avoir heurté des mines marines, alors qu’ils tentaient d’emprunter une route que les Gardiens qualifient d’interdite Iran's IRGC says four tankers ablaze after hitting mines near Strait of Hormuz », Reuters , 4 novembre 2026.'> 1 . Selon le CENTCOM, le commandement militaire américain qui patrouille dans la région et soutient le transit des navires, l’armée américaine a aidé à exporter plus de 1,5 milliard de barils de pétrole depuis cet été. En parallèle de la présence américaine, les exportateurs ont recours à des pétroliers-navettes, qui traversent le détroit avant de transborder leurs cargaisons sur d’autres navires dans le golfe d’Oman. L’incapacité de Téhéran à maintenir un contrôle sur les flux transitant par Ormuz tient également à la dégradation significative de ses capacités. Ces dernières semaines, l’Iran a utilisé des drones sous-marins chargés d’explosifs, a tiré des roquettes antichars (RPG) et déployé des équipes pour fixer des mines-ventouses sur des navires. Ces moyens, qualifiés par l’Institute for the Study of War de « sous-optimaux », sont moins efficaces que les missiles balistiques et de croisière antinavires et les drones utilisés au début de la guerre Iran Update, November 4, 2026 , Institute for the Study of War.'> 2 . Téhéran a également perdu une partie de sa capacité à surveiller le trafic dans le détroit, notamment car ses radars côtiers ont été visés à plusieurs reprises par des frappes américaines. Les Gardiens ont aujourd’hui recours à de petites embarcations qui observent et transmettent la position des navires, alors que l’armée américaine continue de mener des frappes non annoncées, notamment sur l’île de Qeshm, située à l’entrée du détroit, lundi 2 novembre U.S. Strikes Iran’s Qeshm Island as Trump Talks Down War Risks », The Wall Street Journal , 2 novembre 2026.'> 3 . Téhéran continue cependant de bénéficier d’une aide militaire russe : selon des responsables de services de renseignement occidentaux, les deux pays ont encore renforcé leur partenariat depuis le début de la guerre. Plus d’une vingtaine de navires russes ont notamment acheminé vers l’Iran, via la mer Caspienne, des cargaisons comprenant des munitions, des composants de drones et du TNT Russia is shipping explosives to Iran to bolster its missile and drone arsenal in U.S. war », NBC News , 18 août 2026.'> 4 . L’article Téhéran peine à bloquer les exportations de pétrole du Golfe est apparu en premier sur Le Grand Continent .

items.title: Collision between passenger bus, truck near Pakpattan claims 11 lives
items.description: LAHORE: A collision between a passenger bus and truck on Thursday claimed the lives of 11 people and left 33 others injured near Pakpattan. Rescue 1122 said that 11 people had died in the collision. It added that eight people had sustained minor injuries, while 25 others were shifted to the District Headquarter Hospital (DHQ) in Pakpattan. According to a press release by the district administration, the collision occurred on Depalpur Road between a passenger bus travelling from Multan to Kasur and a truck coming in the opposite direction. Upon receiving news of the accident, Deputy Commissioner (DC) Asif Raza and District Police Officer (DPO) Javed Iqbal Chadhar immediately arrived at the scene to oversee rescue operations, working alongside teams from Rescue 1122 and the district administration, the statement said. The three-hour rescue operation used cranes and other heavy machinery to extract passengers trapped in the wreckage. “Given the gravity of the incident, DC Raza declared an emergency at the DHQ Hospital, Pakpattan and summoned additional doctors and medical staff,” the press release added. Later, the DC and DPO visited the hospital to enquire after the injured and review the arrangements for their medical care. DC Raza directed the hospital administration to ensure the provision of “prompt, high-quality medical care” to all the injured. The statement said DC Raza expressed grief at the lives lost and also extended his condolences to the bereaved families. “Extending his best wishes for the speedy recovery of the injured, he directed the relevant authorities to continue providing all possible support for medical treatment and relief operations,” it added. President Asif Ali Zardari expressed “profound grief and sorrow” over the “tragic loss”. A statement on social media said that the president extended his condolences to the bereaved families and prayed for the early recovery of the injured in the accident. Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz also expressed “deep sorrow” over the loss of lives in the accident, according to a handout issued by the province’s Directorate General of Public Relations (DGPR). She directed authorities to ensure the best possible medical treatment for the injured passengers. CM Maryam “prayed for the speedy recovery of the injured passengers and extended her heartfelt sympathies and condolences to the bereaved families”, the statement said, adding that she sought a report on the accident. Separately, National Assembly Speaker Sardar Ayaz Sadiq also extended “heartfelt sympathy and condolences to the bereaved families”. He also prayed for the early recovery of those injured in the accident.

items.title: La Cour constitutionnelle déclare la vacance des sièges des députés nommés au gouvernement
items.description: La Cour constitutionnelle a déclaré vacants les sièges de plusieurs députés à la Chambre des représentants, à la suite de leur nomination au gouvernement. Dans sa décision n° 294/26, rendue le 4 novembre, elle a notamment constaté la vacance du siège de Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri, devenue Cheffe du gouvernement, ainsi que ceux de plusieurs parlementaires ayant rejoint l’exécutif. La décision, consultée par Hespress FR , concerne également Abdellatif Ouahbi, Ryad Mezzour, Mehdi Bensaïd, Azzeddine El Midaoui, Abdessamad Kiyouh, Abderrahim Chahid, Najwa Koukous, Omar Hejira et Rachid Hammouni, nommés membres du gouvernement le 16 octobre 2026. La juridiction rappelle que l’article 14 de la loi organique relative à la Chambre des représentants interdit le cumul entre le mandat parlementaire et la qualité de membre du gouvernement. Cette incompatibilité entraîne la déclaration de vacance du siège du député concerné, à la demande du président de la Chambre des représentants. En revanche, la Cour a déclaré irrecevable la demande concernant Madiha Khayr. Nommée au gouvernement le 16 octobre, celle-ci avait été déchargée de ses fonctions ministérielles le 18 octobre, avant la présentation de la demande du président de la Chambre des représentants, enregistrée le 23 octobre. Dans sa décision, la juridiction constitutionnelle a estimé que la demande du président de la Chambre des représentants concernant le cas de Madiha Khayr n'est « pas conforme à la condition légale requise pour déclencher la procédure de constatation de vacance du siège, ce qui impose d'en prononcer l'irrecevabilité ». La décision revient également sur le cas de Nizar Baraka, qui a gardé son poste de ministre de l'Equipement, de l'Eau et des Forêts, et dont la situation avait fait l’objet d’une décision distincte de la Cour constitutionnelle, rendue le 3 novembre 2026. Cette dernière avait prononcé la vacance de son siège à la Chambre des représentants, où il avait été élu dans la circonscription électorale de Larache. Aussi, la décision porte également sur plusieurs demandes relatives à des démissions de députés. La Cour a constaté que les sièges concernés étaient devenus vacants et a ordonné la notification de sa décision aux parties concernées ainsi que sa publication au Bulletin officiel. The post La Cour constitutionnelle déclare la vacance des sièges des députés nommés au gouvernement appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Équipe d’Algérie : Hemdani dévoile sa liste, sans Luca Zidane et Aït Nouri
items.description: Luca Zidane a-t-il perdu sa place chez les Verts ? Le sélectionneur de l'équipe d 'Algérie de football, Brahim Hemdani , a dévoilé ce jeudi 5 novembre la liste des 26 joueurs convoqués pour la double confrontation face au Togo en éliminatoires de la CAN 2027 (14 et 17 novembre). Le fils de Zinedine Zidane n’y figure pas, au même titre que Rayan Aït Nouri, auteur d’un écart disciplinaire lors du dernier stage. La liste de Hemdani comprend en outre deux nouveaux venus, convoqués pour la toute première fois. Il s'agit de Mohamed Azzi et Abderrahmane Rebbach. De nombreux joueurs absents du dernier stage ont en outre été rappelés. Algérie – Togo : Luca Zidane non convoqué par Hemdani Hemdani a convoqué trois gardiens de but, Mastil et Ramdane qui ont pris part au dernier stage, ainsi que Oussama Benbot qui fait son retour après avoir été écarté à l'issue du Mondial. Benbot a pris la place de Killian Bellazoug. On s'attendait à ce que Luca Zidane retrouve les Verts après avoir manqué les derniers matchs pour suspension, mais Brahim Hemdani en a décidé autrement. Il semble que Zidane ait fait les frais de la politique du sélectionneur qui privilégie les joueurs les plus en forme du moment. En conférence de presse, Hemdani a expliqué la non-convocation de Luca Zidane par ce critère du temps de jeu. Hemdani à propos de Zidane : « Un choix sur un critère sportif » « J’ai fait mes choix sur un critère sportif, sur ce poste-là qui est vraiment particulier. J’avais besoin d’avoir le choix entre trois gardiens qui avaient un maximum de temps de jeu. Les trois sélectionnés ont le maximum de temps de jeu depuis le dernier rassemblement, et c’est la seule raison pour laquelle j’ai tranché en faveur de ces trois gardiens-là », a-t-il dit. Ce qui laisse la porte ouverte à un éventuel retour du fils de Zinedine Zidane lors des prochains regroupements. Aït Nouri écarté, une première pour Azzi et Rebbach En défense, le sélectionneur a éloigné Chergui, Redouani et Aït Nouri et rappelé Rafik Belghali, absent lors du dernier stage pour suspension. Il a aussi convoqué pour la toute première fois Mohamed Azzi, défenseur du CSKA Moscou . L’absence d’Aït Nouri a tout l’air d’une mise à l'écart après son coup de gueule en septembre dernier, même si elle peut aussi s’expliquer par son faible temps de jeu à Manchester City. Bentaleb et Boudaoui, deux importants retours au milieu L'équipe nationale enregistre aussi deux importants retours au milieu de terrain, en l’occurrence Nabil Bentaleb et Hicham Boudaoui qui reviennent de blessure. Titraoui fait lui aussi son retour, tandis que Abderrahmane Rebbach, du Deportivo Alavés, est appelé pour la première fois. Aouchiche et Zorgane ont fait les frais de ces renforts. Pas trop de changements en revanche en attaque où seul Ghedjemis a pris la place de Kebbal. Le reste de la force de frappe des Verts est là avec Amoura, Bakrar, Boulbina, Gouiri, Chiakha, Hadj Moussa et Belloumi. Équipe d’Algérie : la liste des 26 joueurs convoqués Gardiens : Oussama Benbot, Melvin Mastil et Abderrahmane Ramdane. Défenseurs : Jaouen Hadjam, Ramy Bensebaini, Rafik Belghali, Zinedine Belaid, Achraf Abada, Sohaib Nair, Mohamed Azzi et Ahmed Touba. Milieux de terrain : Nabil Bentaleb, Himad Abdelli, Hicham Boudaoui, Fares Chaibi, Ibrahim Maza, Abderrahmane Rebbach et Yacine Titraoui. Attaquants : Mohamed Amoura, Moncef Bakrar, Adel Boulbina, Amine Gouiri, Amin Chiakha, Anis Hadj Moussa, Bachir Belloumi et Fares Ghedjemis. items.title: Prisons Service calls for national policy to support ex-convicts’ reintegration
items.description: The Ghana Prisons Service has called for a comprehensive National Reintegration Policy to address the stigma, discrimination and unemployment confronting formerly incarcerated persons as they seek to rebuild their lives after prison. The Service says the challenges continue to undermine efforts to reintegrate former inmates into society, making it necessary for government, the private sector, families and communities to provide sustained support and employment opportunities. The call was made at the maiden National Ex-Convicts Conference organised by the Crime Check Foundation at the GNAT Hall in Accra on Wednesday, November 4, 2026. Held under the theme, “Rebuilding Life After Prison: Effective Reintegration for a Better Society,” the conference brought together stakeholders to discuss ways of addressing social exclusion and creating opportunities for people returning to society after serving prison sentences. Delivering an address on behalf of the Ghana Prisons Service, the Director of Prisons in Charge of Operations and Facility Management, Mr Benedict Bob-Dery, reaffirmed the Service’s commitment to the rehabilitation and reintegration of inmates. He, however, identified societal stigma, discrimination and unemployment as major obstacles that make it difficult for former inmates to rebuild their lives. He urged stakeholders to move beyond prison-based rehabilitation by creating an enabling environment for returning citizens to secure jobs, gain social acceptance and access post-release support. Mr Bob-Dery said such interventions were necessary to reduce reoffending and promote public safety. Also addressing the conference, the Chairman of the Prisons Service Council, Apostle Ing. Alexander Nana Yaw Kumi-Larbi, highlighted the importance of prison ministry and partnerships with stakeholders in advancing inmate rehabilitation and reintegration. He encouraged participants to support the Service’s Think Prisons 360 Degrees Agenda and embrace the Employing the Returning Citizen Campaign . He stressed that having a criminal record should not become a lifelong barrier to employment and social acceptance, urging society to give formerly incarcerated persons a fair opportunity to rebuild their lives. Some former inmates who shared their experiences at the conference recounted the difficulties they faced after leaving prison, particularly stigma, discrimination and exclusion from economic opportunities. They appealed for greater public support and inclusive opportunities to help returning citizens reintegrate successfully. The event was attended by the Director-General of Prisons (Rtd.), Mr Isaac Kofi Egyir, senior officers of the Ghana Prisons Service and other key stakeholders. The Service’s participation reinforces its position that its mandate extends beyond the safe custody of inmates to include their rehabilitation, reformation and eventual reintegration as productive members of society.

items.title: Petrol price slashed by Rs9.41 per litre, high-speed diesel by Rs5.56
items.description: The government on Thursday dropped the price of petrol by Rs9.41 per litre and that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs5.56, in the fourth consecutive reduction in fuel prices. Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs352.59 per litre, while HSD will cost Rs382.25 on Nov 6 (Friday), according to a notification by the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra). The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel. Under an arrangement announced on Monday for 30 days, oil refineries will contribute to the petroleum levy by bearing a cumulative impact of Rs15 billion, according to the government. This allows a Rs14.71 reduction in the petrol price at the consumer end. Addressing a press conference on Tuesday, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik said efforts were being made to introduce a similar system for liquefied petroleum gas (LPG). Meanwhile, the Jamaat-i-Islami and the government are set to follow up on their recent discussions on possible relief in petroleum prices and hold another round of talks on Thursday, the party said. Rise in fuel prices The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on Feb 28. The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March. Meanwhile, the government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices amid the ongoing Middle East conflict. Under these measures, markets are required to close by 9pm, and fuel allocations for official vehicles have been cut by 50pc for three months. On Sept 13, PM Shehbaz also announced a “ relief scheme ” for users of motorcycles, autos and vehicles of up to 800cc to “alleviate the burden” of rising global oil prices. Previously, on July 17, the petroleum minister announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US. Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel. The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give Ogra the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends. Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes. Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators. Petrol and HSD are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

items.title: Ghanaians hold on to cherished food traditions as Christmas approaches
items.description: As Christmas approaches, families are preparing to celebrate the festive season with meals that bring them together and keep cherished food traditions alive. For many households, Christmas is not just about the celebrations but also the special dishes that have become part of their family traditions. Yet, with the cost of food and festive preparations often a concern, some families are finding ways to maintain their favourite meals without giving up what makes the season special. Speaking in a Christmas series exploring the foods families cannot do without during the festive season, Daniel Thompson said his family would continue preparing eba, describing it as an affordable meal. He said the family might switch from yellow gari to white gari to manage costs, but eba would remain part of their Christmas menu. “We will not stop eating eba because eba is cheap in Ghana. I’ll just change the yellow gari to white gari but I’ll never stop,” he said. For Gordon Amoah, akple remains an important part of his family’s Christmas tradition. He said the family traditionally prepares the meal during the festive season and intends to maintain the practice this year. “Traditionally, my family loves to prepare akple during Christmas and that is our main food. Akple is so important to my family in such a way that we believe that you find so much carbohydrates in akple,” he said. Christiana Ekpe, on the other hand, said fried rice, chicken and salad were the special meals her family looked forward to preparing during the festive season. She described the combination as an important part of their celebrations, making Christmas more memorable. Grace Acheampong also shared her family’s tradition of preparing waakye with chicken, grilled fish, onion, salad, macaroni and gari every Christmas. She said the tradition dates back to her childhood, making the meal particularly special to the family. “We prepare that food because we enjoy it when I was a child,” she said. The accounts highlight how Christmas meals go beyond satisfying hunger, with family traditions, affordability and childhood memories shaping what households choose to prepare during the festive season.

items.title: Coopérative Song-Taaba : Des biscuits pour soutenir les FDS et les VDP au front
items.description: Originaire de la région du Nakambé, la société coopérative « Song-Taaba » de Tenkodogo connaît une grande affluence. Elle présente au salon une gamme de produits transformés mettant en valeur le potentiel des céréales locales. Selon les déclarations de la responsable de la coopérative Song-Taaba, basée au secteur N°1 de Tenkodogo dans la région de Nakambe, Larba Tarnagda Nagalo, la participation à cette 18e édition du Salon International de l'Artisanat de Ouagadougou (SIAO) vise à promouvoir les saveurs de sa région. Elle a affirmé que sa coopérative s'illustre particulièrement dans la fabrication de biscuits modernisés à base de petit mil, de maïs, de riz de Bagré et de sorgho rouge chocolaté. Parmi ces produits, elle met en avant une création spécifique nommée « L'énergie du combat ». Elle a expliqué avoir conçu ce biscuit hautement nutritif pour soutenir les Forces de défense et de sécurité (FDS) et les Volontaires pour la défense de la patrie (VDP). On peut trouver une gamme innovante et variée de céréales transformées et de produits forestiers non ligneux de la coopérative sur son stand. Selon elle, ce repas sec et facile à emporter permet aux combattants de résister plusieurs jours sur le terrain, offrant une alternative plus saine au pain sec ou aux boîtes de conserve. Elle propose aussi aux visiteurs du lait d'arachide prêt à boire, du couscous de maïs jaune, des grumeaux de bouillie de petit mil ou de sorgho rouge, ainsi que du soumbala de néré ou de soja destiné à remplacer les bouillons chimiques sans oublier les huiles (sésame, d'arachide, de balanites, de graines de baobab) et du beurre de karité naturel. La promotrice de la société coopérative « Song-Taaba », Larba Tarnagda Nagalo, promeut le ‘’consommons local’’. Elle a affirmé que les produits de son groupement respectent un planning de fabrication strict garantissant l'hygiène et la qualité. Grâce à cette rigueur, elle signale que les ventes battent des records et que les contacts d'affaires B2B augurent des suites favorables. Julien Zoungrana Crédit photos : Julien ZOUNGRANA

items.title: Ayariga urges residents to keep surroundings clean as AMA deploys 20 tricycles
items.description: The Minister for Local Government, Chieftaincy and Religious Affairs, Mahama Ayariga, has urged residents to take greater responsibility for sanitation by ensuring waste is properly disposed of rather than leaving refuse outside their homes for government authorities to collect. He said keeping communities clean should go beyond maintaining individual homes to include the surrounding environment, stressing that sanitation was a shared responsibility. “Sometimes people clean their home and just put the waste right in front, and then they make it the responsibility of government to come and take the waste right in front of their homes,” he said. Mr Ayariga made the remarks while commending the Accra Metropolitan Assembly (AMA) for procuring 20 tricycles to support waste collection and sanitation activities across its 20 electoral areas. He urged other metropolitan, municipal and district assemblies to emulate the initiative by investing their Internally Generated Funds (IGF) in projects that address sanitation challenges. “I urge your Assembly and others to emulate this example and try and put their IGF to more productive use by making these types of investments,” he said. The Minister also disclosed that the government was working with development partners to construct additional landfill sites, while investing in transfer stations and vehicles to improve waste collection and evacuation. AMA deploys tricycles across electoral areas The Mayor of Accra, Michael Kpakpo Allotey, said the tricycles were procured with the Assembly’s internally generated funds following requests from assembly members for equipment to support sanitation activities in their respective electoral areas. He said the assembly members had asked him to provide the equipment within one or two months, adding that the Assembly fulfilled the request last week. “Any time I have an opportunity to talk, I say it’s not about talking, it’s about action,” he said. The Presiding Member of the AMA and Assembly Member for the Amamomo Electoral Area, Musa Ziyad, said the tricycles formed part of efforts to advance President John Dramani Mahama’s vision of making Accra a cleaner and greener city. He said the equipment would be distributed across the 20 electoral areas to help assembly members respond to sanitation complaints, evacuate accumulated refuse and address problems such as gutters requiring desilting. Mr Ziyad explained that having the tricycles available in the electoral areas would allow assembly members to respond more quickly when residents reported sanitation problems. The initiative forms part of the AMA’s efforts to strengthen community-level sanitation and improve waste management across the capital.

items.title: Commerce avec l’Afrique : l’Algérie s’apprête à inaugurer une zone de libre-échange à Tindouf
items.description: Relier par train à la Méditerranée, Tindouf, dans l’extrême sud-ouest de l’Algérie, sera bientôt dotée d’une zone de libre-échange orientée vers la Mauritanie et les pays de l’Afrique de l’Ouest. La zone de libre-échange de Tindouf sera en effet bientôt opérationnelle. Cet espace qui vise à développer les échanges commerciaux internationaux avec les pays de l’Afrique de l’Ouest, notamment les exportations algériennes vers ces pays, sera réceptionné avant la fin de l’année en cours. C'est ce qu'a annoncé ce jeudi 5 novembre le ministre du Commerce extérieur et de la Promotion des exportations, Kamel Rezig, lors d’une séance de questions orales au Conseil de la nation. Zone de libre-échange de Tindouf : un complexe intégré de 200 hectares Cette zone de libre-échange est un “ projet stratégique ”, a indiqué le ministre. Dans sa description, Kamel Rezig a précisé que le “projet intégr é” s'étend sur une superficie de 200 hectares et comprend six grands entrepôts, de vastes espaces destinés aux exposants, un centre de contrôle des marchandises, une base de vie, des bâtiments administratifs abritant les douanes, les banques et les assurances, ainsi que des infrastructures de services et de sécurité et un centre de santé, “offrant ainsi un environnement de travail complet aux opérateurs économiques ”. La première pierre de cette zone de libre-échange, située à proximité du poste-frontière avec la Mauritanie, a été posée en 2024 par le président de la République, Abdelmadjid Tebboune, et son homologue mauritanien Mohamed Ould Cheikh El Ghazouani. Deux ans après, les travaux d’aménagement sont entièrement achevés, a annoncé Kamel Rezig. Vers la création d’un établissement chargé de la gestion des zones franches Celui-ci a fait état de la coordination des services du ministère avec l’ensemble des secteurs concernés “ afin de mener à bien les procédures de réception définitive et d’entrée en service effectif du complexe, pour qu’il devienne un pôle commercial et logistique central qui soutient la compétitivité des opérateurs et renforce notre présence économique en Afrique ”. Le ministre a indiqué à la même occasion qu’un projet de décret portant création d’un établissement public chargé de la gestion des zones franches se trouve actuellement au niveau du secrétariat général du gouvernement. L’article Commerce avec l’Afrique : l’Algérie s’apprête à inaugurer une zone de libre-échange à Tindouf est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Comedian Russell Brand found guilty by UK court of rape and sexual assaults
items.description: Comedian Russell Brand, once one of Britain’s most high-profile broadcasters and star of several Hollywood movies, faces a lengthy jail term after being convicted in a London court on Thursday of raping a woman and sexually assaulting three more. Prosecutors said Brand, the former husband of US pop singer Katy Perry, was obsessed with sex and used women to satisfy his own desires. One victim said he treated her “like an animal”. Funny and charming when he wanted to be, but also ruthless, calculating and manipulative , the 51-year-old was interested only in getting what he wanted from women, prosecutors told jurors at Southwark Crown Court. “The evidence showed Brand to be a calculated sexual predator, using his growing fame and power to create situations in which he could pursue women sexually, regardless of what they wanted,” senior Crown prosecutor David Roberts said outside court. Brand now faces jail and potentially further action as police said he was still under investigation for two other alleged rapes, one involving a then 16-year-old girl. Brand denied the charges Brand, known for his loquacious manner and flamboyant appearance, had denied all the charges and ever having non-consensual sex, saying the incidents, which dated back more than 20 years, had either been consensual, reinvented or re-imagined. He acknowledged in evidence he had dedicated a lot of his life to “reckless philandering and idiocy” but said sexual consent was fundamental. But, following a four-week trial, the jury found him guilty of rape and three sexual assaults committed between 2004 and 2009. He was acquitted of two other rape charges and an attempted indecent assault. Judge Joel Bennathan said Brand, who was refused bail, would be sentenced on Monday and faced a lengthy prison term. Brand is one of the most prominent celebrities in Britain convicted of sex offences in recent times, after BBC newsreader Huw Edwards admitted making indecent pictures of children two years ago, and entertainer Rolf Harris was found guilty of assaulting young girls in 2014. The case has again raised questions about how the entertainment industry deals with complaints about its stars, and Detective Inspector Laura Nelson, who headed the investigation, said she expected other women to come forward. “I think there are other victims out there and if they want to report that to us, then we’ll of course take it seriously,” she told Reuters . Complainants described maniacal demeanour Prosecutors had said Brand’s offending spanned the years in which he rose from performing stand-up comedy in small venues to becoming a television presenter and Hollywood film star. The court heard tearful and forceful testimony from the six complainants, who are all entitled to lifelong anonymity. None of the women knew one another but all came forward to police in the wake of a TV documentary and press reports in 2023 in which other women made separate allegations against Brand. Those women were not involved in this criminal trial. Giving evidence, the complainants described a sudden change in Brand’s demeanour during their encounters, saying he became wide-eyed and maniacal. One woman said that less than a minute after she met him at a party in a bar, he had grabbed her breasts. Another victim, a self-described fan of Brand, said she had gone to his home for consensual sex, but he had then removed a condom and anally raped her. Afterwards, he had ordered her to clean up the bloody mess on the sheets. Throughout his career, Brand has been open about his battles with drugs and sex addiction, writing about both in his 2007 autobiography My Booky Wook . One witness, a former friend with whom Brand later lived, told the court Brand had bragged that he wanted to sleep with 5,000 women. Brand’s former personal assistant, Helen Berger, who worked for him from 2006 to 2007, said he had “an insane sexual appetite”. “He never seemed happy after sex, more so depressed,” she said in a witness statement. Police say conviction sends clear message Brand rose to prominence in Britain by hosting a spin-off show to ‘Big Brother’ on Channel 4 . During the 2000s, he became a regular fixture on television and radio, and went on to star in a number of films. In 2010, he married Perry, a relationship that, he told the court, brought him “staggering fame”. The marriage ended after 14 months. Nelson said Perry had not been approached as a potential witness, but said she could always come to the police if she had any information. In subsequent years, Brand moved away from mainstream TV and film work, and built a large social media following as an anti-establishment commentator, discussing politics, spirituality and religion. He was baptised as a Christian in 2024, after the allegations first became public. “I hope this conviction sends a clear message that no one is above the law, no matter how famous or powerful they may be,” Detective Superintendent Andy Furphy from London police said.

items.title: Afua Kobi Ampem SHS wins Ashanti NHIS inter-school quiz
items.description: Afua Kobi Ampem Senior High School has emerged as the winner of the Ashanti Regional edition of the National Health Insurance Authority’s (NHIA) inter-school quiz competition, beating Ibadur Rahman Academy SHS and Opoku Ware School. The competition forms part of a nationwide public education initiative aimed at improving students’ understanding of the National Health Insurance Scheme (NHIS), including its benefits, entitlements and operations. Organised under the auspices of NHIA Chief Executive, Dr Victor Asare Bampoe, the initiative involves 48 schools across the country. Participating schools were provided with study materials and sensitisation to strengthen their knowledge of the scheme ahead of the regional contests. Speaking on behalf of the NHIA head office in Accra, Acting Head of Corporate Affairs, Oswald Essuah-Mensah, said the initiative was intended to equip young people with the knowledge to understand and effectively use the scheme. He explained that the sustainability of the NHIS depended on three key stakeholders: the scheme itself, healthcare providers and its members. “The scheme survives on three legs. Basically, we have the scheme itself, we have our providers, and we have you as members,” he said. Mr Essuah-Mensah encouraged the students to become ambassadors of the scheme by sharing information about its benefits with people in their communities. Students highlight learning experience Speaking on behalf of her teammates, Jacqueline Aygabeng of Afua Kobi Ampem SHS expressed excitement over their victory, describing the competition as challenging but rewarding. “We don’t know how to express the joy, but it wasn’t an easy competition. At the end of the day, we give thanks to the Almighty God for being so good to us,” she said. She said preparing for the contest had been challenging because the subject was relatively new to the team, but support from their patrons and fellow students helped them succeed. “The moment of learning it and putting the points in our heads was quite tough because it came our way and we didn’t really have much knowledge about it,” she added. Jacqueline said the competition had broadened her understanding of the NHIS and the benefits available to its members. “I didn’t really know how much NHIS was putting into our healthcare until I joined this competition,” she said. Sixteen winning schools are expected to progress to the zonal competitions, with successful contestants advancing to the grand finale in Accra. Organisers say the initiative is expected to strengthen awareness of the NHIS among students and encourage them to share their knowledge with their families and communities.

items.title: GH¢31bn informal cross-border trade faces hurdles despite AfCFTA commitments
items.description: Informal cross-border trade in Ghana, estimated at GH¢31 billion in the first three quarters of 2025, continues to face significant operational challenges, raising concerns about the country’s ability to fully harness the benefits of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA). Despite its contribution to the economy, small-scale traders, particularly women, are confronted with complex border procedures, undocumented levies, prolonged transit delays, inadequate infrastructure and limited access to trade information. The figures, cited from the Ghana Statistical Service at a stakeholder dialogue in Aflao in the Volta Region, indicate that informal cross-border trade was approximately 54 per cent higher than trade recorded through formal land channels during the period. It also represented about six per cent of Ghana’s total trade, highlighting the economic importance of trading activities that largely operate outside formal channels. However, representatives of cross-border women traders from Elubo, Hamile, Paga, Aflao and Akanu say the challenges confronting them continue to undermine their ability to expand their businesses and participate fully in formal trade networks. At the dialogue, the traders reported experiences of arbitrary charges, harassment, confiscation of goods and lengthy delays at border crossings. They also identified inadequate information on approved trading procedures and the absence of effective complaint mechanisms as factors discouraging their participation in formal trade. The Ghana Revenue Authority (GRA) Customs Division says it is taking steps to simplify border procedures through the introduction of the Simplified Goods Declaration (SGD) system, which allows traders to declare their goods and pay the required duties through simplified processes. A representative of the Customs Division, Joseph Mills, said the authority was working to streamline border operations to facilitate trade. However, stakeholders noted that existing AfCFTA and ECOWAS simplified trade arrangements are yet to provide specific protections for small-scale traders. National Coordinator of the AfCFTA National Coordination Office, Dode Seidu, said there was a significant gap between the commitments under the continental trade agreement and the everyday experiences of traders at Ghana’s borders. He called for simplified, gender-responsive trade procedures, improved border infrastructure, accessible trade information and stronger coordination among border agencies. The stakeholder dialogue, organised by the Africa Capacity Building Foundation (ACBF) in collaboration with the Ghana National AfCFTA Champions, also identified the need to formalise informal trading activities without creating additional barriers for small-scale operators. A Joint Stakeholder Action Plan developed at the meeting proposes the digitalisation of border processes, including digital travel itineraries and the publication of approved fees. The Ghana Immigration Service and GRA Customs have been assigned responsibility for advancing these measures, while the Ministries of Trade, Agribusiness and Industry, and Gender, Children and Social Protection are expected to support infrastructure improvements, gender-responsive training and trader empowerment. The Paramount Chief of Aflao, Torgbui Adzonugaga Amenya Fiti V, also called for the development of Aflao into a modern logistics and commercial hub to create more opportunities for women, young people and businesses in border communities. The dialogue was convened under the African Development Bank-funded CADAST programme, implemented with ESAMI-TRAPCA, to align Ghana’s trade and border governance commitments with the realities confronting traders. Stakeholders say addressing the challenges through transparent fees, simplified procedures, improved infrastructure and accessible grievance mechanisms will be critical to ensuring that small-scale traders benefit from the opportunities offered by AfCFTA.

Cross-border traders allege harassment, illegal levies without formal complaint channels
items.description: Women engaged in cross-border trading in Ghana continue to face harassment, arbitrary charges, confiscation of goods and security risks, with no formal mechanisms to report abuses at the country’s borders, stakeholders have revealed. The concerns were raised at a stakeholder dialogue on safe and inclusive trade at Ghana’s borders, organised by the Africa Capacity Building Foundation (ACBF) in collaboration with the Ghana National AfCFTA Champions at Aflao in the Volta Region. Representatives of women traders from Elubo, Hamile, Paga, Aflao and Akanu recounted experiences of undocumented levies, harassment by officials, prolonged transit delays and the confiscation of their goods. They also identified limited access to information on approved border procedures and the absence of structured feedback mechanisms as major obstacles to reporting violations and accessing formal trade protections. The Ghana Revenue Authority (GRA) Customs Division acknowledged the challenge, with its representative, Joseph Mills, disclosing that there are currently no formal channels specifically established to address harassment of traders at the borders. He said affected traders could, however, register complaints at the office of the sector commander. The stakeholders at the meeting The National Cross-Border Women Traders Association also confirmed the absence of official complaint mechanisms, explaining that many traders prefer reporting their grievances to the association rather than the Customs and Immigration services. The situation, stakeholders say, exposes a gap between Ghana’s commitments under the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) and the everyday experiences of small-scale traders, particularly women. The AfCFTA National Coordination Office’s National Coordinator, Dode Seidu, called for simplified and gender-responsive trade procedures, stronger coordination among border agencies, accessible trade information and effective complaint channels. The dialogue also identified the need for formal representation of informal traders in national AfCFTA policy discussions to ensure their concerns inform decisions on border governance and trade facilitation. As part of efforts to address the challenges, stakeholders developed a Joint Action Plan that includes establishing a border-level grievance-redress mechanism to provide women traders with safe and accessible channels to report violations. The plan also proposes an institutionalised platform for informal trader representation in national AfCFTA policy processes and coordinated reforms involving relevant government institutions. The Ghana Immigration Service and GRA Customs have been identified as responsible for improving the digitalisation of border processes, including digital travel itineraries and the publication of approved fees. The Ministry of Trade, Agribusiness and Industry, together with the Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection, will support improvements in border-community infrastructure, gender-responsive training and trader empowerment. The Paramount Chief of Aflao, Torgbui Adzonugaga Amenya Fiti V, called for the establishment of a permanent Aflao Border Stakeholders Committee to strengthen collaboration among security agencies, traders and traditional authorities. He also advocated the publication and digitalisation of all approved border fees and the introduction of effective complaint mechanisms at the various border crossings. The stakeholder dialogue was convened under the African Development Bank-funded CADAST programme, implemented in collaboration with ESAMI-TRAPCA, to align continental and regional trade commitments with operational realities at Ghana’s borders.
